stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi Akhilesh Yadav UP Elections 2027 Alliance: ‘बंद मुट्ठी लाख की, खुली तो खाक की’, अखिलेश यादव और राहुल गांधी, दोनों को ही यह समझना होगा। अगर उन्हें 2027 में योगी आदित्यनाथ को चुनौती देनी है। लेकिन जिस तरह के बयान समाजवादी पार्टी और कांग्रेस की तरफ से आ रहे हैं, उससे तो यही लगता है कि दोनों ही दल मुट्ठी खोलने को आतुर हैं। सरल शब्दों में कहें तो दोनों अपने बूते उत्तर प्रदेश की सत्ता पर काबिज होने का ख्वाब देख रहे हैं। इसमें कोई दोराय नहीं कि राहुल गांधी के कार्यक्रमों में भीड़ उमड़ रही है। अखिलेश यादव की फैन फॉलोइंग भी बढ़ी है, लेकिन कांग्रेस या समाजवादी पार्टी का अपने दम पर सरकार बनाना, फिलहाल तो मुश्किल नजर आता है। बीजेपी के पास एक तरफ पीएम मोदी की लोकप्रियता है, तो दूसरी तरफ सीएम योगी की बुलडोजर बाबा की छवि। इसके अलावा, योगी के कार्यकाल में यूपी में काफी काम हुआ है। खासकर उत्तर प्रदेश ‘गुंडई’ राज्य का दाग धोने में कामयाब रहा है। ऐसे में राहुल या अखिलेश के लिए अकेले बीजेपी का सामना आसान नहीं होगा।

stories.summary: A 23-year-old woman was allegedly gang-raped in Amroha by a sub-inspector, a head constable and two CRPF personnel. The woman is from Haryana. It is alleged that CRPF Inspector Lalaram brought her to Amroha. Head Constable Mohit was also with him. The two took the woman to a farmhouse near Jhulpuri village. The farmhouse is reportedly owned by independent MLA Umesh Sharma, who represents the Khanpur seat in Uttarakhand. On Tuesday night, Sub-Inspector Sanjay Tomar and Head Constable Pramod Malik also reached the farmhouse. All four allegedly held a drinking party before entering the room and assaulting the woman. Sanjay Tomar and Pramod Malik are posted at Hasanpur police station. The woman called police officers during the night and informed them about the incident. However, the police allegedly kept the matter under wraps throughout the day. Action was taken after pressure mounted. A case was registered against all four accused at 4:20 pm. After this, SP Lakhan Singh Yadav appeared before the media and gave details about the arrests and the incident. However, the accused were not presented before the media. SP Lakhan Singh Yadav said the woman had undergone a medical examination. The accused are being questioned. Later in the evening, Moradabad DIG Muniraj G. reached Amroha and spoke to the SP about the case. Now, know the full sequence of events… The woman is from the Fatehabad police station area in Haryana. According to the FIR, she spoke to a female friend on September 20. She was called to Sonipat to meet CRPF Head Constable Mohit. Mohit is a resident of Saurang in Muzaffarnagar district. Brought to Amroha by car, picked up a friend on the way According to the woman, she reached Sonipat at around 1 pm on September 21, where she met Mohit. Mohit took her to Meerut in his Brezza car. On the way, he picked up his associate, CRPF Inspector Lalaram Yadav. Lalaram is a resident of Khatan Kheda village under Naharot police station in Alwar district, Rajasthan. “They entered the room and raped me” The woman said Mohit and Lalaram took her to Hasanpur in Amroha on Tuesday. They met Sub-Inspector Sanjay Tomar at the gate of Hasanpur police station. All of them then went to Jhulpuri farmhouse in Hasanpur, where two rooms were booked. Mohit, Sub-Inspector Sanjay Tomar and Lalaram lay down in one room. After some time, Hasanpur police station constable Pramod arrived with food and alcohol. He is a resident of Kheda Mastan village under Fugana police station in Muzaffarnagar. The four men sat together in one room, had food and drank alcohol. I ate my food sitting in my room. After some time, Mohit, Lalaram Yadav and Sanjay Tomar entered my room. The three raped me. Pushed him out and locked the room The woman said the three accused left the room after the alleged rape. When the fourth accused, Pramod, entered the room, she pushed him out and locked the door from inside. She then searched for the Amroha police number on Google and informed the police. SP says information was received at night, all accused arrested SP Lakhan Singh Yadav said police received information from a woman late on the night of September 22 that she had been assaulted. Police immediately reached the spot and took details of the incident. The investigation found that the woman had come to Amroha with two acquaintances, Mohit and Lalaram. The two had come to meet their friend Sanjay. According to the woman's statement, she had sexual relations with the accused during this time. A case was registered on her complaint, and all the accused were arrested and are being questioned. Know about the MLA who reportedly owns the farmhouse… MLA Umesh Sharma's farmhouse is located near Jhulpuri (Rajhoha) village in the Hasanpur Kotwali area of Amroha, on the link road leading to Gajraula. The lavish agricultural farm is also known as "D D Brothers Farmhouse". It came into the spotlight in 2022 after a theft was reported there. A call was made to the MLA to seek his response on the matter, but he did not answer. His PA Zubair Kazmi said, “MLA ji is undergoing therapy. He was at a rally in Khanpur today, due to which he is suffering from back pain.” According to his PA, information about the entire matter will be given at the MLA's office at 11 am on Thursday. From sting operation to launching a political party, know Khanpur MLA's story Umesh Kumar won the Khanpur seat as an independent candidate by a large margin in the 2022 Uttarakhand Assembly elections. Before becoming an MLA, he was an investigative journalist and CEO of a news channel. He gained national recognition through a sting operation carried out during the Harish Rawat government. Formed a new party, wife made president In June 2026, Umesh Kumar held a large public meeting in Roorkee and announced his new party, the 'Jan Nirman Party'. He appointed his wife, Sonia Sharma, as the party's national president. The party aims to contest elections in Uttarakhand as well as western Uttar Pradesh. Recently, he inducted former Congress leader Rao Moin into his party and began expanding his political base in Khanpur and surrounding areas. Had flowers showered from a helicopter, conducted an aerial survey of rivers In August 2026, MLA Umesh Kumar continued his annual tradition. He had flowers showered from a helicopter on Kanwariyas and devotees at Har Ki Pauri in Haridwar and Jatashankar Temple in Khanpur. He also conducted an aerial survey of rivers and embankments in the Khanpur Assembly constituency to assess the flood situation. MLA himself became a fraud victim, cheated by Ranchi conman In June 2026, Umesh Kumar made headlines across national media after he was allegedly cheated of ₹4.50 lakh. A fraudster from Ranchi allegedly duped him on the pretext of selling an old vintage 'Morris car' and took the money. A case was registered at Rajpur police station in Dehradun in connection with the matter. Organised mass wedding for 151 daughters Apart from political activities, Umesh Kumar is also known in the area for his social initiatives. In December 2025, he organised a grand mass wedding ceremony for 151 underprivileged daughters in Khanpur, attended by several prominent personalities. The farmhouse has 20 dogs, high-tech cameras installed Khanpur MLA Umesh Sharma's farmhouse is spread across several acres. It has more than 20 dogs described as aggressive. The farmhouse is equipped with high-tech technology and HD cameras. Entry to the farmhouse is reportedly allowed only with the MLA's approval. Several cricketers, including Suresh Raina and Mohammed Shami, have visited the farmhouse. IAS and IPS officers also stay there.

The accident occurred at around 12 p.m. on Wednesday. Fortunately, no one was injured in the accident. See two pictures... Read what is shown in the video... Tanker breaks through divider and overturns on the other side City SP Ran Vijay Singh said that the tanker was travelling from Haryana to Rudrapur. The driver turned the tanker while trying to avoid a person crossing the road on the Ramganga bridge in Moradabad. During this, the tanker went out of control, broke through the divider, crossed to the other side and overturned. Police used a crane to set the tanker upright. The vegetable ghee scattered on the road was also cleared, after which traffic on the highway was restored to normal. No one was injured in the accident.

stories.title: Brij Bhushan-Ramdev settle dispute after ₹50 crore notice:Yoga guru says Patanjali ghee 100% pure; ‘We are no drug-addict, cannabis-smoking sadhus’
stories.summary: The four-year war of words between former BJP MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh and yoga guru Baba Ramdev appears to be coming to an end. The two met at the Constitution Club in Delhi on Wednesday, where they sat together on a sofa, spoke and were seen smiling and laughing. Later, Baba Ramdev held a solo press conference at 3.30 pm. The yoga guru said that he had met Brij Bhushan Singh and that some misunderstandings based on hearsay and videos had been cleared after their conversation. According to Baba Ramdev, Brij Bhushan Singh greeted him during the meeting and said, “We always respect saints and Sanatan, and we also respect the work you are doing for the country.” Brij Bhushan Singh had been calling Patanjali ghee fake since 2022. Recently, Acharya Balkrishna, president and Ayurvedacharya of Patanjali Yogpeeth, sent him a ₹50-crore defamation notice, accusing him of damaging the company’s reputation. The matter was heard in the Madhya Pradesh High Court on September 15. Brij Bhushan had said he was ready to go to jail but would not seek bail. Four major points made by Baba Ramdev 1. Brij Bhushan called three days ago Baba Ramdev said Brij Bhushan Singh had called him three days earlier. According to Ramdev, Brij Bhushan said over the phone, “Let’s end everything that has been said till today,” to which he replied, “End it.” Ramdev said Sant Rajkumar Das of Shri Ram Vallabh Kunj in Ayodhya and Dau Ji Maharaj had earlier spoken to each other. Both saints told Brij Bhushan that Swami Ramdev was doing significant work for Sanatan Dharma, Bharat Mata and yoga, and asked why the two were involved in a dispute. 2. Patanjali ghee and medicines are not fake Baba Ramdev also responded to questions raised over Patanjali’s cow ghee and medicines. He said Patanjali’s cow ghee was not fake and that none of the company’s medicines were fake either. He also spoke about his life as a monk, saying that he had not taken sanyas for drugs. Ramdev said he lived the life of a monk with authenticity and transparency. 3. Vow to serve Bharat Mata until his last breath Ramdev said his life was dedicated to the commitment to serve Bharat Mata. He said that from waking up at 3 am until going to bed at 10 pm, his life remained devoted to this purpose. 4. No land or bank balance in my name Speaking about his personal life, Baba Ramdev said that there was not an inch of land or even a rupee in bank balance in his name. He said that even when he had nothing, he had remained “akincan”, and despite receiving much from India and around the world today, he still sleeps on a mat spread on the floor. Brij Bhushan called him the ‘emperor of adulterated goods’ and mocked him as ‘Kana’ Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, who was an MP from Uttar Pradesh’s Kaiserganj seat, had repeatedly made personal attacks against Baba Ramdev. In Bahraich, he had called Baba Ramdev the “emperor of those who make adulterated goods”. He had said the issue was not limited to Patanjali ghee. According to him, fake paneer was available in villages and shops selling fake food products had opened at every street corner. He had said that if someone ordered 10 quintals of paneer, 10 quintals could be made available within a day. He described fake food products as a major problem. Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh had said he opposed all manufacturers of adulterated and fake products. He also said Patanjali had several brands spread across India and abroad and claimed that its products had been banned in several countries. He had urged the government to pay attention to the issue. Following these statements, Patanjali Foods Limited filed a ₹50-crore defamation claim against Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh. The case relates to his public statements about the quality of Patanjali ghee and was heard in the Madhya Pradesh High Court. Brij Bhushan had to apologise On August 17 last year, Brij Bhushan had said in Balrampur, “Ramdev is Kana, the person in whose name he is earning and making a living. The history of Maharishi Patanjali is also connected to Gonda.” He later apologised for the statement. Explaining his remarks, Brij Bhushan had said, “I had made a statement during the Lok Sabha election. After that, Acharya Balkrishna Bhatt called me and said I was a fool. We also responded to him, and that is when our dispute began. “In Balrampur, I was talking about the history of Gonda, Balrampur and the Devipatan division. During this, Maharishi Patanjali was mentioned. “I remembered that when Baba Ramdev had set out on his Swadeshi Yatra, he had mentioned the birthplace of Maharishi Patanjali in Gonda and promised that he would work for its development. He had made this promise to the people. “In that context, I remembered Baba Ramdev. Some words came out of my mouth. Later, I realised that I should not have said that.”

stories.title: Father asks cops for chocolate after daughter cries:Held her hostage in room for 7 hours; told SP, ‘Come closer, I’ll shoot’
stories.summary: In an incident in Azamgarh, four people were killed, an encounter took place and a seven-month-old infant died, with the entire family falling apart within seven hours over a dispute surrounding the Mahamrityunjaya chant. The accused, Arvind, allegedly opposed the chant, while his wife and mother insisted that it be performed; police said Arvind killed his wife and two priests in the dispute. After this, he held three children hostage in a room and stayed there. For seven hours, more than 300 police personnel, including the ADG, tried to persuade him, but he did not open the door. He threatened them, saying, "SP sahib, do not come near me, or I will shoot everyone." When the girl began crying from hunger, he opened the window and said, "My daughter is crying from hunger; bring chocolate for her." The SP had the police bring a chocolate worth ₹500 and gave it to the girl. The ADG then told Arvind, "We are with you; do not panic." After some time, Arvind said again through the window, "You people leave, or I will kill my children." Meanwhile, he shot his son. The personnel fired smoke grenades and tear gas, broke down the door and entered the room. Arvind fired six rounds at the police. He was killed in retaliatory action. The dead included Arvind's wife Babita (40), son Shaurya (9), seven-month-old daughter, priest Mahendra Pathak (60) and Akhilesh Mishra (55). How did the children remain in the accused's custody for seven hours? How did the police carry out the entire operation? Let's read... 6 pm - Returned from the market and carried out the crime Arvind's elder brother, Sunil Singh, was murdered eight years ago. The family suspected that his spirit was troubling Arvind. Therefore, Kamla Devi and Babita had called priests to conduct a puja. Four priests, including Mahendra Pathak (60), Akhilesh Mishra (55) and his son Himanshu, arrived to conduct the puja. Arvind had been opposing the puja from the first day. He opposed it again on Monday. The police arrived then as well, counselled him and left. According to the police, Tuesday was the final day of the puja. At around 6 p.m., after the aarti following the recitation of the Mahamrityunjaya mantra, the priests were preparing for the purnahuti. Villagers began taking the prasad and returning home. Meanwhile, Arvind returned from the market. He then began arguing with his wife. When the priests conducting the puja approached him to reason with him, he began hurling abuses. He asked the priests for their Aadhaar cards. The priests said, "We are priests. Why would we carry Aadhaar cards? We are neither hawkers nor from Nepal or Bangladesh." But he remained adamant. He reprimanded the priests and began driving them out of the house. He said, "Leave this place immediately, or I will beat you up." As soon as she heard this, his wife Babita angrily confronted him. She said, "What are you saying? It is not right to insult the priests." Hearing this, Arvind began arguing with his wife. In anger, he pulled out a revolver and shot her in the head. As soon as she fell to the ground, the priests began fleeing. Priest Mahendra Pathak had managed to run only five steps from the place of worship when Arvind ran after him and shot him in the head a second time. After this, priest Akhilesh Mishra and his son Himanshu reached the house's main gate and began opening it. Just then, Arvind came running from behind, shouting. Seeing him in anger, Himanshu jumped over the wall of the house and fled, while his father, Akhilesh Mishra, remained inside. Arvind fired the third bullet at his head. He collapsed on the road there. Hearing the sound of gunfire, villagers reached the spot. On seeing the villagers, Arvind waved his revolver in the air. As a result, the villagers stopped at a distance. After committing three murders, Arvind locked himself inside a room in the house along with his three children. Police arrived at 7 p.m.; killer said, ‘Call the captain’ Ahraula station in-charge Ramkishore Sharma and the Dial 112 team arrived at around 7 pm after being alerted by neighbours. The police entered through the main gate and found the bodies of three people lying inside the house. The accused, Arvind, had locked himself in a room with the children. He was peering out through the room's window. The police then told him, "Open the door." However, Arvind did not open it. He told the police, "Call the SSP first, then we will open the door." At around 7:15 pm, police captain Dr Anil Kumar and SP Rural Chirag Jain arrived. They told Arvind, "Open the door. We will not do anything to you." At 8 pm, sister arrived; he said, ‘Why have you come here?’ At 8 pm, the police called Arvind's sister, Sadhna. From outside the house, Sadhna called out to Arvind, saying, "Brother, open the door." Arvind became angry as soon as he saw his sister. He said, "Why have you come here? Don't you have a home?" His sister replied, "This is my home too." Arvind shouted from inside, "This is not your house. Go away." His sister said, "There is a little girl inside. Bring her out and give her to me. She must be hungry. Let me feed her milk." Arvind showed her a revolver and drove her away. At around 8:30 p.m., Arvind's mother, Kamla, was called. Kamla tried to reason with him as well, but Arvind did not open the door. He said, "My brother has been murdered. No one helped." 9:30 p.m. - SP calls in the SOG and forces from 10 police stations At 9 p.m., the SSP said, "Arvind, don't panic. We are with your family." Arvind then said, "It has been eight years. My brother was murdered. I have not received justice. The accused are roaming free. My life is in danger." Arvind then told the SSP, "Call the SDM and tehsildar, and then we will open the door." The SSP called the SDM. By around 9:30 p.m., the SDM and tehsildar had also reached the spot. Meanwhile, the SSP called the SOG and forces from 10 police stations to the spot. The PAC also arrived. The police force surrounded his house from all sides. When the SDM reached the spot, the SSP told Arvind, "The SDM is here. Now open the door. Don't be afraid. We will listen to whatever your demand is." ADG arrives at 11:30 p.m., says, ‘Let the children go’ Even then, Arvind did not open the door. He said, "Call the ADG now; only then will we open the room door." At 11:30 p.m., Varanasi ADG Naveen Arora arrived. The ADG told Arvind, "We are with you. Do not panic. Send the children outside. We will not harm you. You will be heard. Open the door and come outside." But he did not come out. Midnight: Told SP to bring chocolates Arvind said through the window, "SP sir, my children are hungry. My daughter is crying. Get chocolates for them from the village shop." The SP ordered chocolates worth ₹500 for the children. Then the SP said, "Come out now." The accused replied, "We will not come out now. It is very late. My daughter and children have gone to sleep. I do not leave the house at night." "I will open the room in the morning, when it is light, and come out. If I come out now, I will be killed." Hearing this, the police captain said, "Nothing like that will happen. You and your children will remain safe. Open the door and come out." ATS arrived at 12:30 a.m.; an encounter took place at 1 a.m. At around 12:30 a.m., 25 ATS commandos arrived from Varanasi. The team surrounded the house from all sides. Meanwhile, Arvind said, "You people leave, otherwise I will kill my children." Just then, the sound of gunfire came from the room. After this, the ATS and SOG went on alert. The team fired stun grenades and tear gas into the house. Then around 20 personnel and the captain entered and broke open the room's door. As soon as the police entered, Arvind opened indiscriminate fire at them while issuing a warning. He fired six rounds. The police also retaliated. One bullet hit him. The police took Arvind and his son to the district hospital in an injured condition, where doctors declared Arvind dead at 3:30 a.m. While Arvind was firing, his infant daughter fell from his lap. She too died during treatment in the afternoon.

stories.title: Woman breaks down crying before Akhilesh Yadav:Says, ‘Daughter’s wedding in November, bulldozer demolished our house’
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav held a press conference in Lucknow on Wednesday. During the event, a woman from Ayodhya broke down in tears in front of Akhilesh. She said her house did not fall within the road-widening area, yet it was demolished in a bulldozer action. A woman named Preeti Chauhan, while crying, said, “My daughter's wedding is in November. A bulldozer was brought to my house at 1.30 am. Everything I had is gone. All my belongings and jewellery are gone. I have nothing left now. I have come here to plead for help. My children are sitting outside.” Sapna Rajpal said she was not even given enough time to vacate her shop and house. She was asked to remove her belongings within half an hour. Freezers and refrigerators were kept in the warehouse, but the bulldozer was still brought in. “Now we have nothing to eat. We do not even have money for medicines. We had never seen such oppression before,” she said. Akhilesh said, “No one can become an obstacle to Lord Ram and the development of Ayodhya. If the Samajwadi Party government is formed, we will make Ayodhya the world's most modern and ‘world-class’ city. But the present government is working to uproot poor people and shopkeepers in the name of development.” The administration had carried out the bulldozer action in Ayodhya for the widening of the 14-Kosi Parikrama Marg. Eleven houses and shops in the Janaura Naka area were demolished. The action, which began during the day, continued until late at night. Major points from Akhilesh's press conference 1. ‘Fake signatures were used to remove 100 votes at a time, the election was stolen’ The SP chief expressed concern over alleged electoral fraud. He said an application was submitted in Sultanpur to remove the votes of 100 people using the forged signature of a person who could not even sign himself. According to the rules, no more than five votes can be removed at a time, but votes were allegedly being removed in batches of 100 using the fake signature of a person named ‘Dashrath’. 2. ‘If BJP wins, there will be no elections after 2027’ Akhilesh said, “A major conspiracy is being hatched to destroy democracy in the country. If BJP is not stopped this time, this will prove to be your last election. After that, your right to vote will also be taken away. In other words, there may be no elections at all after 2027.” 3. Fairness cannot be expected from the Election Commission He said, “In 10 months, two Election Commissioners raised 14 objections over wrong decisions. But nothing happened. When even the Election Commissioners are not being heard, what will happen to the common person? This is a crime aimed at destroying democracy. In such a situation, fairness cannot be expected from the Election Commission. Future elections should also not be conducted by them.” 4. Votes of SP supporters were identified and removed Akhilesh said, “Even in the 2022 Assembly election, the votes of SP supporters were identified and removed. In the by-elections too, dishonesty was carried out on a large scale by getting officials posted arbitrarily. We were forced to go carrying shrouds.” 5. ‘BJP is nobody's well-wisher; people will run the bulldozer’ Taking a jibe at BJP, Akhilesh Yadav said the BJP government was nobody's well-wisher. He said that in Meerut, action had been taken against BJP's own leaders who had been celebrating action against others. The SP chief alleged that murders and loot were taking place every day in Uttar Pradesh. He said digital fraud was taking place in the state capital, but the government's focus was only on allegedly plotting to win elections through the transfer and posting of officials. 6. Election Commission and BJP completely exposed Akhilesh said, “You are committing the theft, you are being caught, and you are looking for someone else. The Election Commission and BJP have been completely exposed. In the coming days, the people will use their right to vote to bulldoze this government out of power forever.”

stories.title: Woman strangled to death in Bijnor:Body burnt in field, 18-month-old girl found crying beside it; admitted to hospital
stories.summary: A woman's partially burnt body was found in a field in Bijnor, Uttar Pradesh. A one-and-a-half-year-old girl was crying beside the body, wrapped in a gamcha. According to the police's preliminary investigation, the woman was murdered elsewhere. Her body was then brought to the field and set on fire. The incident came to light at 7 a.m. on Wednesday. A villager who had gone out for a morning walk heard the child crying. When he went closer, he saw the child lying beside the woman's body. He then raised the alarm and called people from the surrounding area. Women picked up the child and held her in their arms. They then called the police. The police took the child to hospital and sent the body for a post-mortem examination. The woman has not yet been identified. She is believed to be between 20 and 25 years old. The incident took place in Alampur Adwa village in the Noorupur police station area. See 3 pictures... Know the full details... Dhyanpal Singh, a resident of Gohawar Jait, owns a field on the road from the Ramganga feeder canal to Roshanpur village. He said, "I had gone out for a walk at around 7 a.m. As soon as I reached near my field, I heard a child crying. When I went closer, I saw a woman's body lying there." Her baby girl was beside her and was crying. I picked up the child and then called the women who were out for their morning walk. I handed the child over to the women and informed the police. The women fed the child milk and calmed her down. Shortly afterwards, on receiving the information, station house officer Pravej Kumar reached the spot with a police team. The forensic team was called in after that. Station house officer Pravej Kumar said, "Around 40 per cent of the woman's body had been burnt. Her abdomen and legs had suffered burns. There were no injury marks on her face. The woman was wearing toe rings. This suggests that the child was hers." Meanwhile, villagers say that the killers may have had a close relationship with the girl, as they left her alive.

stories.title: Junior Engineer beaten during power inspection in Bijnor:Seated on cot and slapped, punched; official had caught them running heater by tapping power cable
stories.summary: A junior engineer was beaten up by people while he had gone to inspect electricity connections in Bagadpur village in the Chandpur police station area of Bijnor on Friday. Three to four people initially argued with him before suddenly attacking him. When the junior engineer remained seated on a charpoy, the accused did not let him get up and continued raining punches and slaps on him. A video of the assault emerged late on Tuesday evening. Police have registered a case against the accused based on the junior engineer's complaint and begun an investigation. See two visuals Now, here is the full story A departmental team of 10 employees, led by JE Sudeep Kumar Sharma, arrived in Bagadpur village at around 3 p.m. last Friday to inspect electricity connections. The village is around 50 km from the district headquarters and has a powerhouse where JE Sudeep Kumar Sharma is posted. During the inspection, the team found a cut in the incoming cable of the electricity meter at the home of a farmer, Sanjeev. An investigation found that electricity was being stolen through the cut to run a heater. Electricity was also being used in the shops built outside the house through the same cut. A dispute broke out when the team began videographing the scene. JE allegedly held hostage and beaten It is alleged that an argument first broke out, after which Sanjeev, along with Navneet, the village head's husband, began beating the JE with the help of some farmers. He was then held hostage. Before the JE could understand what was happening, villagers began beating him. Meanwhile, when the staff members who had accompanied the JE started recording a video, their mobile phone was snatched and they were made to delete the video. They then continued beating the JE for around 15 minutes. A villager recorded a video of the incident, in which several people can be seen surrounding and assaulting the JE. The JE was held hostage for around an hour. The police then reached the village, freed the JE and took him to the police station. FIR against 20 to 30 people, including the pradhan's husband JE Sudeep Kumar Sharma submitted a complaint at Chandpur police station. The police registered a case against 20 to 30 unidentified people, naming Sanjeev, Sanjeev's son, pradhan's husband Navneet, Sudhanshu, Ankit and Mohit. The police said the case was being investigated on the basis of the viral video and the complaint.

stories.title: Mayawati replaces nephew Akash with Ishan:Makes him national coordinator, No. 2 post in BSP; party chief active ahead of polls
stories.summary: BSP supremo Mayawati on Wednesday appointed her younger nephew Ishan Anand as the party’s national coordinator. The post was earlier held by her elder nephew Akash Anand. Mayawati had removed Akash from the post of national coordinator, the party’s No. 2 position, on September 3. Five days later, she expelled him from the party. Mayawati, who has repeatedly changed her decisions over the role of her successor and family members in the party, had called a meeting of the national executive. This was her second meeting in 20 days. Mayawati reached the BSP office in Lucknow at exactly 11 am. She was accompanied by her younger brother Anand Kumar and younger nephew Ishan Anand. Mayawati went straight to her chair. Ishan Anand stood beside her with his hands folded for quite some time. When Mayawati placed her hand on his back, he touched her feet. There was also a change in the seating arrangement in the hall. Until now, four to five chairs were usually placed beside Mayawati. However, on Wednesday, chairs were placed in the front row for state president Vishwanath Pal, general secretary Satish Chandra Mishra, vice-president Anand Kumar and Ishan Anand. Prince Yukesh Singh, son of late MLA Umashankar Singh, also attended the meeting. Around 400 BSP office-bearers took part in the meeting. State presidents and state in-charges from different states, along with district presidents and divisional coordinators from Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand, also attended. stories.title: UP launches govt ‘Bharat Taxi’:Yogi takes ride; Deputy CM says, ‘Don’t chase jobs, drive cab for 4 hours’
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath launched the government-backed cab service 'Bharat Taxi' in Lucknow on Wednesday. During the event, he said, “The results of the formation of the Ministry of Cooperation are now being seen. People whom no one used to think about, such as taxi drivers, will now become part of Bharat Taxi with registration and zero commission.” He said, “Until now, taxi drivers were not given any security. They were left to fend for themselves. Today, when a driver gets 'Bharat Taxi' written on his car, he will feel proud that it is a taxi for the whole of India. He will also have the assurance that he is getting a social security guarantee of ₹5 lakh.” Both passengers and drivers will benefit from Bharat Taxi. The service will also provide auto-rickshaw, car and bike services. Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak said, "Don't worry, adopt Bharat Taxi. Bharat Taxi means your own money, your own motor and your own driver.” Referring to driving cabs for private companies, he said, "Don't get caught up in jobs and foreign companies, drive your own taxi for four hours." The Chief Minister also launched the portal for the 'Krishak Samriddhi Yojana' and the 'Setu App' for fertilisers and seeds. He handed over loan cheques to farmers and taxi certificates to drivers. After flagging off Bharat Taxi, the Chief Minister also took a ride in one of the cabs. Yogi's key points 1. Earlier, even buffaloes were stolen from carts Yogi said, “Before 2017, forget two-wheelers and three-wheelers, if someone travelling in a bullock cart stopped somewhere for tea, their buffalo would disappear. Taxi tyres would be stolen. Earlier, you could not tell whether the road was in a pothole or the pothole was in the road. There would be curfews for months and riots would take place. If goons of the ruling party travelled in a taxi, they would beat up the driver and steal the vehicle.” He said farme₹used to get loans from cooperative banks at an interest rate of 11%, which had now been reduced to 6%. A loan facility of up to ₹10 lakh has been made available, he said, adding that the government would also provide loan facilities to 5 lakh small and marginal farmers. He said, “This means the double-engine government has now become the strength of farmers and the poor.” 2. Giving weapons to corrupt hands will only lead to destruction He said, “Under the leadership of PM Modi and Home Minister Shah, cooperation is becoming a symbol of the country's prosperity. Cooperation is an important part of our daily lives. However, success depends on who is in charge of the cooperative sector. If you hand over weapons to negative and corrupt hands, they will only cause destruction.” He added, “If power is placed in the hands of people with positive thinking, the security of society and the nation will be strengthened. Cooperation is a double-edged sword, with both a good and a bad side. With good leadership, cooperation becomes a reason for progress.” 3. If there is a theft, arrangements are in place to deal with it at the next crossing Yogi said, “There are no curfews now, there are no riots and there is no theft now because 14 lakh CCTV cameras have been installed. If a theft takes place somewhere, arrangements are in place to deal with it at the next crossing.” He said farmers used to migrate and were frustrated and disappointed, while middlemen dominated the system. “In 2017, we first waived loans worth ₹36,000 crore for our farmer brothers,” he said. He said the Saryu Nagar project took 50 years to complete because farmers were not part of the agenda of the earlier governments. He said the Arjun Sahayak project, Bansagar project and Middle Ganga project faced a similar situation. The double-engine government provided irrigation facilities to an additional 24 lakh hectares of land, he said, adding that this had helped increase farmers' incomes. “Earlier, the motor installed on farmers' fields would be stolen. Today, we have made irrigation free. We are providing free electricity,” he said. Deputy CM says there was a 'country-made pistol culture' under SP government Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak said, “Earlier, the Cooperation Department had become sick. No matter how much money was invested in it, it remained in losses. Now CM Yogi and Cooperation Minister JPS Rathore have made it profitable.” He said, “There was a 'katta culture' under the SP government. People used to keep a katta in their pockets and earn money. Now there is a pen culture, and people are earning through the pen.” Union Minister of State for Cooperation Murlidhar said, “Bharat Taxi and the CM Krishak Samriddhi Yojana are being launched in Uttar Pradesh. Bharat Taxi is also being launched in Gorakhpur, Varanasi and Prayagraj today. Bharat Taxi is an initiative of our Ministry of Cooperation, which has changed the shape of the cooperative sector in just a few years.” Understand the benefits of Bharat Taxi in 4 questions and answers How can its service be used? Bharat Taxi's app is similar to Ola and Uber and can be downloaded from app stores. The app is available in Hindi, Gujarati, Marathi and English. What will drivers gain? Drivers will receive 100% of the earnings from every ride. They will only have to pay a daily, weekly or monthly fee, which will be kept very nominal. Government support and trust: Bharat Taxi is part of a government initiative, so there will be greater transparency and regulation. Ola and Uber are entirely private companies. Peak hours: During busy periods, fares on Ola and Uber can suddenly increase, causing inconvenience to passengers. This will not happen with Bharat Taxi. An effort will be made to keep fares stable. The aim is to provide passengers with an affordable and reliable service.

stories.title: Taj Mahal trip turns costly for American couple:2 kids snatch purse packed with dollars and passports; CCTV trail reaches Mathura
stories.summary: Two children stole a purse containing dollars from an American tourist couple in Agra. The purse contained $2,750, along with essential documents and passports. In Indian currency, the amount is worth more than ₹2.5 lakh. After the incident, the tourist couple filed a case at the tourism police station. CCTV footage showed two boys running away with the purse. They had gone to a medical store to buy medicine According to information, the American tourist couple had come to visit Agra with their friend, Nguyen Phuon. They were all staying at the Trident Hotel on Fatehabad Road. At around 5 p.m. on 19 September, the couple went to a medical store in the Tajganj area to buy medicine. After buying the medicine, they paid for it and placed the purse in a bag hanging from the shoulder. Meanwhile, two boys aged nine and 12 at the shop saw them putting money in the purse. It was reported that both boys followed the couple from the shop and began asking them for money. The couple ignored them and continued walking. The chain of the bag hanging from the woman's shoulder had been left open. On their way back to the hotel, the two boys surrounded them again. While engaging them in conversation, one of the boys took the purse from the bag, and both fled the scene. The purse contained more than ₹2.5 lakh The couple told police that the purse contained $2,750, ₹2,000 and their passports. As soon as the information was received, the tourism police examined recordings from CCTV cameras installed around the scene. The footage showed two boys fleeing with the purse. ACP, Taj Security, Yatendra Nagar, said police had traced the boys to Mathura railway station with the help of CCTV footage. The investigation revealed that the two boys lived on the pavement near the Taj Nagari Metro station. The police team is trying to apprehend them and recover the dollars.

stories.title: ₹4.25 crore GST evasion detected in Varanasi:SIB raid lasted 4 days; action against railway contractor and tent house
stories.summary: The Special Investigation Branch (SIB) of the Uttar Pradesh State Tax Department has detected GST evasion worth ₹4.25 crore near the Banaras Locomotive Works (BLW). The SIB has taken action against a railway contractor and a tent house. To uncover the evasion, the SIB continued raids for four days and disclosed the findings late at night. The investigation team raided the area near BLW on the night of 18 September. The operation continued until the night of 22 September. The team has not yet released the names of the contractor or the tent house. Tax paid by concealing manpower supply The SIB investigation has revealed that the railway contractor's firm undertakes civil construction work and supplies manpower to DLW through the government e-marketplace. In the return filed for the financial year 2025-26, the firm concealed the manpower supply. The firm did not file its return for 2026-27, even though it was paid more than ₹5.50 crore between April and August 2026. The tax payable on this amount is more than ₹1 crore, which has not yet been deposited. ₹4.25 crore evasion According to SIB officials, the firm obtained input tax worth ₹36 lakh through fake bills. The investigation revealed tax evasion of around ₹4.25 crore. During the action, the contractor also deposited ₹46 lakh and said the remaining amount would be paid soon. Tent house firm also committed fraud According to GST officials, the investigation found irregularities in the documents of the catering and tent house company operating on the same premises. The firm's GST registration was cancelled in March 2026. It had not filed any returns since July 2025. Even so, it was carrying out business on a large scale. The firm had conducted business worth ₹2 crore to ₹2.5 crore from 2022-23 onwards. This is illegal, which is why action is being taken.

stories.title: 3 people missing in Sai river in Lucknow:Wives of 2 are pregnant; one married 2 years ago; went for Ganesh Visarjan
stories.summary: Three people went missing in the Sai River, which flows through Lucknow, on Tuesday evening. They had gone to immerse a Ganesh idol in the river. A crowd gathered at the spot as soon as people learnt about the incident. The SDRF, along with the police, reached the site after being informed. A search is underway for the three people who went missing in the river. The families of the three missing people are also present on the riverbank. Two of their wives are pregnant. The families allege that the SDRF team is searching in only one place. They say this is reducing the chances of finding them alive. The incident took place near the Jabraila bridge in Mohanlalganj. People from Sisendi village, 5 km away, had arrived here at 5 p.m. to immerse a Ganesh idol. A 35-year-old man named Dheeraj then went into the deeper part of the Sai River and began to drown. Forty-year-old Hariprasad entered the river to save him, but he too began drowning. During this, 22-year-old Pramod also entered the river. After that, there was no trace of the three men. Four pictures related to the incident- Three youths still missing after 6 hours Even by 11 p.m., around 6 hours after the incident, there was no trace of the three people. Anita, the wife of missing man Dheeraj, alleged that despite considerable time having passed, no net had been put in the river. A search operation is currently being conducted using one boat. The search does not appear to be progressing quickly. Six local divers and SDRF teams join the search The SDRF team is searching for all three people in the river. Six local divers are also involved in the search alongside the SDRF. The SDRF team reached the spot about 40 minutes after receiving information about the accident and began the search operation. The team includes around 20 constables, along with SI Ritesh Sachan. The team is searching for the people who drowned in the river using a boat, hooks, life jackets and other flood rescue equipment. A police team is also present at the spot. ADM FR, SDM Akash Singh and ACP RK Singh had also reached the spot. Families in turmoil, condition of both men's wives poor The families of Hariprasad and Dheeraj, who went missing in the Sai river, have been in turmoil since news of the accident emerged. Hariprasad's wife, Shyamawati, is pregnant. Their family has a 12-year-old son, Nihal, and a 10-year-old daughter, Nihalika. Meanwhile, Dheeraj married Anita around two years ago. Anita is also around three months pregnant. Dheeraj's mother, Deepa, is also part of the family. Pramod was a resident of Hira Kheda, which falls under Sisendi village. All three worked as labourers to support their families. Following the accident, the three families are in mourning, while their relatives sit by the river, hoping to find their loved ones. Police officers tried to reason with the people Family members present at the spot accused the police administration of delaying and being negligent in the search operation. Police officers explained the situation to them. An officer said, "Please do not worry. The SDRF team is searching in the direction of the river's current. They are highly experienced. No one is sitting idle. Everyone who is here is engaged in the operation."

stories.title: One accused in Agra foetal sex determination case absconding:4 of 5 arrested; Sonipat team raided with decoy pregnant woman
stories.summary: Action has been taken against five accused in connection with foetal sex determination testing at Sanskar Hospital and Trauma Centre in Itaura, Agra. Four of the accused have been arrested, while one remains absconding. Police are conducting a continuous search and search operation to arrest the absconding accused. A joint team from Sonipat and Agra is investigating the case. According to the chief medical officer, further action will be taken against the hospital and those found guilty based on the investigation report once it is submitted. A pregnant woman was used as a decoy to lay the trap The Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) team from Sonipat had laid a trap to catch the foetal sex determination gang. The team used a pregnant woman from Sonipat as a decoy and got her to contact members of the gang. She was made to speak to the gang members to obtain information about the sex of her unborn child. The gang members took the decoy woman to different locations throughout the day. At around 5 p.m., she was brought to Sanskar Hospital and Trauma Centre in Itaura. During this time, the team, which had been prepared in advance, raided the hospital and took action. Chinese wireless ultrasound machine seized During the raid, the team seized a Chinese-made portable wireless ultrasound machine. It has a wireless probe that does not need to be connected to the machine with a cable. An ultrasound can be performed by connecting a tablet or smartphone to the machine via Wi-Fi. The team took the machine into custody for examination. Hospital operating without registration According to CMO Dr Arun Srivastava, Sanskar Hospital and Trauma Centre was being run by Bhanu Pratap, a resident of Saiyan. The hospital was not registered. No doctor was found at the site either. The hospital was operating from three rooms. A board advertising an ICU facility had also been put up there. The investigation revealed that Bhanu and Pradeep had rented the building from Manju, a resident of Shamsabad, around two months ago. Sanskar Hospital and Trauma Centre was being run from the same building. It has also emerged that an application had been submitted to register the hospital. Hospital had operated from the building before The building in which the hospital was being run has three shops on its first floor. Boards stating that the shops were available for rent have been put up. It has emerged that a hospital had previously operated from the same building in the name of Thakur Das. Machine connected via Wi-Fi The portable ultrasound machine that was seized has a wireless probe. It does not need to be connected by wire. A tablet or smartphone is connected to the machine via Wi-Fi. An ultrasound can then be performed. Four arrested, search under way for one accused Five accused have been identified in the case. Four of them have been arrested, while one remains absconding. Police are conducting continuous raids to arrest him, and search operations are being carried out at possible hideouts. Teams from Sonipat and Agra are jointly investigating the entire case. According to the CMO, further action will be taken against the hospital and those found responsible in the case on the basis of the investigation report once it is released.

stories.title: Azamgarh man who killed wife, son, 2 priests shot dead:Angry over puja; 7-month-old girl who fell from his arms also dies
stories.summary: The accused who allegedly killed his wife, son and two priests in Azamgarh, Uttar Pradesh, was killed in an encounter. Fearing arrest, he took his three children hostage inside a room. Seven hours later, he shot his son. After this, the ATS and SOG killed the accused, Arvind Singh (42). During the hostage situation, his seven-month-old daughter had fallen from his lap. She also died during treatment on Wednesday afternoon. Arvind's family now consists of his mother Kamla Devi (70) and daughter Pari (5). The incident took place in the Ahiraula police station area, around 50 km from the district headquarters. According to police, the family suspected that Arvind was being troubled by the spirit of his brother Sunil. His wife and mother had therefore arranged for a Mahamrityunjaya chant to be performed. Arvind was angry about this. At around 6 pm on Tuesday, he argued with his wife over the issue. He said, "Your brother died because of you. Now you are creating a drama here." He then asked the priests for their Aadhaar cards and got into an argument with them. In a fit of anger, he brought a licensed revolver from the room and shot his wife and the two priests. He then took all three children hostage inside the room. After receiving the information, forces from 10 police stations reached the spot, after which Arvind threatened to kill the children. As the situation worsened, 45 personnel from the ATS and SOG were called in. The team continued trying to persuade him to surrender. At 1 am, he fired at his child. The team used smoke grenades and tear gas before breaking down the door and entering the room. Arvind fired six rounds at the personnel with his revolver. He was killed in the retaliatory action. The deceased, apart from Arvind, have been identified as his wife Babita (40), son Shaurya (9), priest Mahendra Pathak (60) and Akhilesh Mishra (55). The bodies have been brought home after the post-mortem, and preparations for the last rites have begun. Police personnel have been deployed outside the house. Brother was killed eight years ago, had been Balasaheb Thackeray's gunner Arvind, a resident of Shambhupur Gahji village, did not have a job. His family included his wife Babita, mother Kamla Devi (70), daughter Pari (5), son Shaurya and seven-month-old daughter. Eight years ago, his brother Sunil was shot dead by his cousins Manish and Avinash. According to the account, Arvind's wife Babita was allegedly having an affair with Manish. After learning about it, Sunil filed a complaint against Manish alleging theft and molestation. Sunil had served as Balasaheb Thackeray's gunner.

stories.title: CM Yogi to inaugurate state women’s shelter today:Built in Gorakhpur at ₹8 crore cost; can house 100 women
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi will inaugurate the newly constructed building of the Government Women's Shelter Home in Gorakhpur today. He will then inspect the under-construction Government Observation Home (Juvenile). The Government Women's Shelter Home building has been constructed in Chargawan, near the Agriculture Department's seed warehouse, at a cost of ₹8 crore 5 lakh 42 thousand. The building has the capacity to accommodate 100 women. Along with accommodation, it also has other necessary facilities. The Government Women's Shelter is a protective and residential institution run under the Department of Women and Child Welfare. The primary objective behind establishing these shelters is to provide safe accommodation, protection and necessary support to women affected by domestic violence, in need, facing difficult circumstances, having lost their way or dealing with other social and family-related difficulties. Before inaugurating the state-run women's shelter, the Chief Minister will inspect the observation home under construction for juveniles. The State Observation Home (Juvenile) is being built in Chargawan, near the Agriculture Department's seed warehouse, at a cost of ₹14 crore 87 lakh. It will have accommodation for 100 juveniles. The campus will also have a separate block for the Juvenile Justice Board. Construction is expected to be completed by February 2027. Chief Minister to attend the seven-day Shrimad Bhagwat Katha at Gorakhnath Temple Chief Minister Yogi will also attend the inaugural programme of the seven-day Shrimad Bhagwat Katha at Gorakhnath Temple. The event is being organised to mark the 57th death anniversary of late Mahant Digvijaynath and the 12th death anniversary of late Mahant Avaidyanath. Storyteller Rajend Das, the head of Malookpeeth in Vrindavan, will narrate the Shrimad Bhagwat Katha to devotees.

stories.title: Teacher Nishat’s couple dance with colleague:Boyfriend angry after seeing them hold hands; killed her, died by suicide 16 days later in Lakhimpur
stories.summary: A video from a Teachers’ Day programme at Children’s Academy School in Lakhimpur Kheri has surfaced days after teacher Nishat Fatima was murdered at the school on September 21. The video shows Nishat performing a couple dance with her colleagues and appearing cheerful during the programme. Police probe past relationship and growing distance The video has raised questions about the events leading up to the murder. Police investigation has revealed details of an alleged past relationship between Nishat and Saud Ansari, as well as growing differences between the two in recent times. It has also been reported that Saud had watched the Teachers’ Day dance video. However, police are still investigating whether the video had any direct connection with the murder. See three pictures from the dance... Police probe Saud’s reaction to Nishat’s Teachers’ Day dance video Saud Ansari was reportedly upset by Nishat Fatima’s dance performance with a fellow teacher at the school’s Teachers’ Day programme. Nishat and Saud had allegedly been in a relationship for a long time, and their families had reportedly known each other for years. However, the two had grown distant over the past few months. Around this time, Saud began posting emotional messages on social media. Police are now investigating whether Saud had watched the Teachers’ Day dance video and, if so, what his reaction was afterwards. The possible connection between the video, his reaction and the subsequent events remains under investigation. Nishat and Saud’s families had known each other for around 10 years According to local residents, Nishat Fatima’s family had previously lived as tenants in a house owned by Saud Ansari’s family. As a result, the two families had known each other for around 10 years and remained in contact over the years. Nishat had been working as a teacher at Children’s Academy for around a year. Local residents said Saud would sometimes drop her at school and also pick her up after work. Teacher murdered at school as children and parents were nearby Saud Ansari allegedly murdered teacher Nishat Fatima and later died by suicide on September 21. As the school was conducting examinations that day, the premises were crowded with students and teachers. Panic spread after the shots were fired. The incident took place around the time the examination was ending, when many parents were waiting outside the school gate. Police personnel who arrived after the incident evacuated the building. The children were reportedly terrified and began crying when they saw their family members. Many left their lunch boxes and water bottles behind as they rushed out of the school. Case registered against Saud and his parents Police also registered a case against Saud Ansari, his father Qayum Ansari and his mother based on a complaint filed by Nishat’s brother. The complaint alleges that the family had pressured Nishat to marry Saud. How did the accused come in contact with the teacher, and why did he commit the crime? Read the full story in 4 points 1- Nishat’s family once rented Saud’s house, where their conversations began Saud Ansari lived in the Naurangabad area, while Nishat Fatima’s family lived in Hidayat Nagar, around 1 km away. Saud’s father, Qayum Ansari, works at the District Industries Office, while his elder brother, Dawood Ansari, runs a sofa and mattress shop. Saud had completed his B.Com and was pursuing a B.Ed. Nishat’s father, Iliyas, works in Mumbai. Her elder brother, Shadab Akhtar, is preparing for the PCS examination, while her younger brother, Anas, is also studying. The family originally belongs to Sultanpur and moved to Lakhimpur with Iliyas around 12 years ago. Initially, the family rented a house owned by Saud’s family. This was where Saud and Nishat first began talking. A few days later, Iliyas had a house constructed and the family moved there. However, Saud and Nishat continued to remain in contact. 2- Saud pressured Nishat to marry him despite her refusal Nishat travelled by auto every day to teach at Children’s Academy School in the Shahpura Kothi area. Local residents said that until a few months ago, Saud would sometimes drop her at school and pick her up on his motorcycle. However, the two had reportedly stopped speaking to each other in recent months. Nishat’s brother, Shadab, alleged that Saud frequently harassed his sister and pressured her to marry him, but she refused. He said the family had tried several times to reason with Saud and had also complained to his parents, but his behaviour did not improve. 3- Saud reached school with two pistols and confronted Nishat According to eyewitnesses, Saud arrived at Children’s Academy School on Monday morning carrying a bag containing two country-made pistols and five cartridges. Students were taking their examinations at the time. When the examination ended at around 11.30 am, Nishat was taking the children out through the school gate. Saud allegedly approached her and began speaking to her. An argument soon broke out between them, and the two continued arguing as they moved towards the first floor. A heated quarrel then took place in the corridor outside Room No. 11. According to the account, Saud took out the pistols and handed one of them to Nishat. 4- Saud threatened another teacher before shooting Nishat and himself Hearing the commotion, a Class 2 teacher rushed towards the corridor to help. Saud pointed a country-made pistol at her and threatened to kill anyone who intervened. The teacher then locked herself and the children inside a classroom for safety. When Nishat reportedly tried to escape, Saud opened fire at her. He then shot himself. Saud posted a final Instagram message minutes before his death Saud had been posting emotional and self-focused messages on his Instagram account for the past few months. Just minutes before his death, he posted an Instagram story referring to his possible death and asking people to delete his photographs and messages. In the post, he wrote: “Assalamu alaikum, everyone. If I die suddenly, I request all of you to remove my photographs from your phones and social media accounts. Delete my messages and report my Facebook account. Nothing in this world is permanent. Since we have come into this world, we will certainly have to leave it. After my death, please do not look at or post my photographs. Pray for me; InshaAllah, this will help me. Forgive me if I have hurt you, knowingly or unknowingly. When you hear that I am no longer alive, do not say or post ‘RIP’. I am a Muslim, so please say, ‘Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un.’ I am proud to be a member of the ummah of Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him). Allah Hafiz!”

stories.title: Which side will educated UP youth lean?:Clear picture to come 3 months before Assembly polls; MLC election to show political mood for 2027
stories.summary: A month before the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, polls have been announced for 11 Legislative Council seats under the ‘Shikshak’ and ‘Snatak’ quotas. The contest is being viewed as a major 'litmus test' for the ruling BJP and the main opposition Samajwadi Party (SP). Both parties have been preparing to win these seats for the past year. Unlike a general election, the electorate here will comprise educated young people, 'Shikshak' and others who have been 'Snatak' for at least three years. The results could therefore indicate the political preferences of the state's educated and younger voters. Know the 11 seats going to polls Of the 11 Legislative Council seats for which elections have been announced, five are 'Snatak' seats and six are 'Shikshak' seats. More than 10 lakh voters to decide the contest More than 10 lakh voters will exercise their franchise in this 'mini-mandate'. To register as a 'Snatak' constituency voter, a person must have held a degree for at least three years. In the 'Shikshak' constituencies, only 'Shikshak' who are currently teaching can vote. Personal outreach, not rallies, will drive the campaign Senior journalist Ratanmani Lal says the format of this special Legislative Council election is very different from general elections. Roadshows and public rallies by senior leaders and ministers do not have much impact in these constituencies. Instead, personal outreach, messaging and political networks are the biggest tools. 'Shikshak' and 'Snatak' vote according to their own views and priorities. SP and independents have won in BJP strongholds The ruling party has some advantage in this election, but the results have also produced surprises in the past. In the 2020 MLC elections, the SP won the Varanasi 'Snatak' seat, despite Varanasi being Prime Minister Narendra Modi's parliamentary constituency. In the Gorakhpur-Faizabad 'Shikshak' seat, from Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's home region, the BJP did not field a candidate. The 'Shikshak' Group candidate won the seat. This is why neither party is taking any seat lightly. BJP has been preparing for MLC elections for a year BJP spokesperson Sameer Singh says the party began preparing for the Legislative Council elections a year ago. The BJP has already announced candidates for five seats, while candidates for the remaining seats will be announced soon. Singh says the BJP will win more seats this time and claims that young people, 'Shikshak' and women are all with the party. He says these groups will teach the SP a lesson. Meanwhile, SP MLC and candidate from the Allahabad-Jhansi 'Snatak' constituency, Dr Man Singh Yadav, says the election will be a contest between the public and the SP on one side and the BJP on the other. He describes it as an election of educated voters and alleges that the BJP shut 26,000 schools and irregularities took place in the recruitment of 69,000 'Shikshak'. What impact will it have on the 2027 election? Senior journalist Ratanmani Lal says the election is not merely a way to elect 11 MLCs but will also help shape the political atmosphere ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. According to him, if the BJP increases its number of seats, it will send a message that the state's educated youth and 'Shikshak' are satisfied with the Yogi government's policies. If the SP gains an advantage in these constituencies, it would gain a psychological boost just before the 2027 election. The results will also give both parties an opportunity to identify their shortcomings and fine-tune their election strategies over the next two months. SP fields candidates on all seats, BJP and Congress announce five each

stories.title: Owaisi seeks alliance, SP-Congress call him ‘vote katwa’:Fear of split in Muslim votes or bid to protect secular image; what will AIMIM do now?
stories.summary: AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi has held five public meetings in Uttar Pradesh since June 2026. After rallies in Bahraich, Bijnor, Saharanpur and Moradabad, he addressed a rally in Kanpur on September 20. While his speeches drew applause from supporters, strong opposition to him has also begun to emerge. The Samajwadi Party and Congress have called him a 'vote cutter' and 'BJP's B-team'. Congress MP Imran Masood says Owaisi's decision to contest the Uttar Pradesh elections will benefit the BJP. Meanwhile, SP MLA Hasan Rumi and former SP MLA Irfan Solanki say Owaisi has failed to understand Uttar Pradesh's political mood. The question now is whether the opposition to Owaisi is merely a political attack or whether it stems from the fear of a split in Muslim votes. Read the full report... Congress says defeating BJP with Muslim votes alone is impossible Congress MP from Saharanpur Imran Masood says the Opposition's main objective is to remove the BJP from power. However, he said this cannot be achieved on the strength of Muslim votes alone. He said, The political atmosphere in Telangana and Uttar Pradesh is completely different. Even if Owaisi wins 4-5 seats through his rhetoric, ultimately it will be the BJP that forms the government. When the BJP comes to power, Muslims suffer the biggest loss. SP alleges Owaisi received a 'package' from BJP SP leaders have also taken a strong stand against Owaisi. Kanpur Cantt MLA Hasan Rumi made a serious allegation, saying that whenever efforts are made to strengthen Muslims, AIMIM is brought into the fray after being given a 'package' by the BJP. He said Owaisi's politics had already been exposed in Bihar and West Bengal. In Bengal, he sought votes in the name of Babri but then disappeared from the scene, he alleged. Expert says Muslim community also has doubts about Owaisi According to senior journalist and Muslim affairs expert Naved Shikoh, the possibility of Muslim votes getting divided because Owaisi entered into the electoral field cannot be ruled out. In the 2022 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, Owaisi's AIMIM claimed to have fielded candidates in 100 seats. The party secured around 0.43% of the votes and did not win a single seat. After the experience of Maharashtra and Bihar, sections of the Muslim community in Uttar Pradesh are also looking at Owaisi with suspicion, Shikoh said. A sizeable section believes that he has entered the fray mainly to cut into the SP-Congress vote, he added. Owaisi's entire focus on western UP After its poor performance in 2022, AIMIM has made a major change to its strategy this time. Instead of merely contesting elections, the party is focusing on strengthening its organisation. The party launched its election preparations from Bahraich in June 2026. Owaisi's particular focus is on Muslim-majority districts in western Uttar Pradesh, including Saharanpur, Moradabad, Bijnor, Muzaffarnagar, Rampur and Amroha. At his Kanpur rally, Owaisi adopted a relatively softer stance towards Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD) chief Jayant Chaudhary. Although the RLD is currently allied with the BJP, Owaisi's approach is being seen as an attempt to work around the political equations in western UP. What will Owaisi do if SP-Congress refuse to join hands? Aseem Waqar, who left Owaisi and joined the Congress, said, On the one hand, Owaisi calls the SP and Congress enemies of Muslims, and on the other, he pleads with them to join hands. How can these two things happen at the same time? According to political analysts, the deadline set by Owaisi is unlikely to have any impact on the SP and Congress. This leaves Owaisi with three options: SP says it keeps away from extremism SP spokesperson Mohammad Azam says the party maintains equal distance from all forms of extremism. He said alliances are not formed through statements made from rally stages; they are decided through discussions between the top leaderships of the parties. Statements made from the stage, he said, are merely political rhetoric. AIMIM spokesperson Shadab Chauhan said, We are not begging for seats. We are talking about respect and our share. In Bihar, Congress and RJD were arrogant. We had asked for six seats, but they did not give them to us. We won five seats and showed them. In UP too, talks are not happening because of Akhilesh Yadav's arrogance. Our fight is against the BJP, but we will not become anyone's sidekick at the cost of our existence. SP-Congress keeping a close watch on Owaisi's every move Senior journalist Naved Shikoh says gathering crowds at Owaisi's rallies is one thing, but converting that support into votes is another. The Muslim voter in Uttar Pradesh has now become very cautious, he said. According to him, voters are aware that the direct contest in the state is between the SP-Congress alliance and the BJP. He said, If Owaisi fields candidates in 200 seats, they may not win, but by cutting 2,000 to 5,000 votes, they could certainly upset the SP-Congress's prospects in 20 to 25 seats. This is why the SP and Congress are keeping a close watch on Owaisi's every move.

stories.title: MLC elections from MLA quota likely soon:10 seats fall vacant in January; polls may be held 2 months early due to Model Code
stories.summary: Elections to 10 Legislative Council seats under the MLA quota may be held in November-December. The terms of the sitting members are set to end on January 30. With the Model Code of Conduct likely to come into force in January because of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the elections to these seats could be held one or two months earlier instead. The Election Commission has already announced elections in October for 11 seats under the teachers' and graduates' constituencies. An official from the Chief Electoral Officer's office said MLAs vote to elect members to the Legislative Council seats that are falling vacant in January. The Model Code of Conduct is likely to come into force in the first or second week of January ahead of the Assembly elections. In such a situation, MLAs would not be able to vote. Therefore, the elections are likely to be held in November-December so that the existing MLAs can elect the new members. At present, the BJP has the numbers required to win eight MLC seats. The party is therefore likely to seek elections to these seats before the Model Code of Conduct comes into force. BJP to lose one seat, SP set to gain Elections to the 10 seats falling vacant were held in January 2021. At that time, the BJP had 304 MLAs and the Samajwadi Party had 47. A candidate needed the support of 31 MLAs to win one seat. Based on this strength, the BJP won nine seats and the SP one. At present, the BJP has 256 MLAs, and the SP has 101. If the 33 MLAs of the BJP's alliance partners, three unaffiliated MLAs and two MLAs of Raja Bhaiya's Jansatta Dal Loktantrik are also included, the total comes to 294. Based on this strength, the BJP is set to win eight seats and the SP two. The Bahujan Samaj Party does not have a single MLA in the Assembly. Therefore, its candidate would not even be able to file a nomination without the support of either the BJP or the SP. BJP preparing to field 2-3 time MLCs in Assembly elections According to BJP sources, central leaders have reached a consensus that workers who have already served two or three terms as members of the Legislative Council or Rajya Sabha should not be given another term. Instead, they should be given a chance to contest Assembly and Lok Sabha elections. The BJP has previously fielded national general secretary Bhupendra Yadav from Rajasthan's Alwar and former Union minister Dharmendra Pradhan from Odisha's Sambalpur in Lok Sabha elections. A party functionary said that if the same formula is applied to the Legislative Council elections, several senior leaders may have to contest Assembly elections to remain members of the legislature. Now, know which faces could get another chance... Kunwar Manvendra Singh Kunwar Manvendra Singh is serving his second term as a member of the Legislative Council. He was earlier a member from 2000 to 2006. He is currently also the Chairman of the Legislative Council. Manvendra served as an MLA from the Garautha seat in Jhansi from 1985 to 1989. He is around 74 years old. The decision on whether the party will give him another term or promote a young member of his family will be taken at Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's level. Swatantra Dev Singh Jal Shakti Minister Swatantra Dev Singh is a member of the Legislative Council for the third time. He first served as an MLC from 2004 to 2010 and then from 2017 to 2021. Swatantra Dev Singh is considered a senior party leader and has a strong hold among the Kurmi community. The party may field him from a Kurmi-dominated seat in Bundelkhand in the upcoming Assembly elections. However, the final decision will be taken by the state and central leadership. Arvind Sharma Energy Minister Arvind Kumar Sharma became an MLC for the first time in 2021. Sharma is from Mau district, which has a sizeable Bhumihar population. A close aide of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the decision on whether Sharma will be sent to the Legislative Council again or fielded in an election will be taken at the Prime Minister's Office level. However, as Sharma is serving his first term as an MLC, the party may give him another opportunity. Dharampal Prajapati Minister of State (Independent Charge) Dharampal Prajapati is also serving his second term as an MLC. He was first made an MLC in 2017. In September 2021, he was inducted as a Minister of State during the second cabinet expansion of the Yogi Adityanath government's first term. In the Yogi government's second term, he was again made Minister of State for Home Guards. Given his influence among the Prajapati (Kumhar) community, Dharampal could be made a Legislative Council member for a third term. However, there is also speculation that he could be fielded from a seat in the Braj region. Ashwini Tyagi Former BJP state minister Ashwini Tyagi is serving his first term as a member of the Legislative Council. He was sent to the Council with the backing of Cabinet Minister Swatantra Dev Singh and former organisational general secretary Sunil Bansal. During the Lok Sabha elections, he was made in-charge of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's constituency, Varanasi. Modi won the election, but his victory margin fell significantly. Tyagi currently holds no position in the central or state BJP teams. The party is considering replacing him with state minister Basant Tyagi as a Legislative Council member. Govind Narayan Shukla Former state general secretary Govind Narayan Shukla became a member of the Legislative Council for the first time in 2021. Shukla had continuously held a position in the BJP's state team since 2014. Although he did not find a place in the state team this time, he was made in-charge of the state party headquarters because of his experience. He is considered close to national general secretary (organisation) BL Santosh and also has good relations with state general secretary (organisation) Dharampal Singh. As a result, Shukla could be given another opportunity. Salil Bishnoi Former BJP state vice-president Salil Bishnoi did not find a place in Pankaj Chaudhary's team. He is serving his second term as an MLC. He has also contested elections from Kanpur's Aryanagar and Sisamau seats but lost both times. Party sources believe Bishnoi may be dropped this time and a new face could be given an opportunity. Dharmendra Singh Dr Dharmendra Singh has been appointed as the party's state vice-president for a second consecutive term. In 2021, he was the BJP's Gorakhpur region president. It was during that period that he was made an MLC with Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's backing. Given his proximity to CM Yogi, Dharmendra Singh could be given another opportunity. Surendra Chaudhary Surendra Chaudhary became an MLC in 2021 with the backing of Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya. In the 2017 Assembly elections, the BJP had given him a ticket from Prayagraj's Soraon seat. However, following an alliance with Apna Dal, the seat went to the ally and Chaudhary had to withdraw his nomination

stories.title: 2 priests shot dead in Azamgarh, wife also killed:Asked people coming for puja to show Aadhaar cards; husband locked himself inside house
stories.summary: In Azamgarh, a husband shot dead his wife and two priests on Tuesday evening. He carried out the killings during a religious ceremony. The husband asked the priests conducting the ceremony for their Aadhaar cards, after which he began arguing with both of them. The husband angrily retrieved his licensed rifle from a room and then opened fire on the two priests and his wife. All three died on the spot. After the incident, the accused husband locked himself inside the house. As soon as the police were informed, forces from several police stations reached the spot. The incident took place in Shambhupur Gahji village in the Ahiraula police station area. See two pictures... Full incident in detail now Arvind Singh, a resident of Shambhupur Gahji, reached home at around 6 p.m. on Tuesday. Present at the house were Pandit Mahendra Pathak (60), a resident of Patkhauli village; Akhilesh Mishra (55), a resident of Chhitauna Bhatauli village; his son Himanshu Mishra; another priest; his wife Babita Singh (40); his mother Samla Devi (70); his daughter Pari (5); his son Lakkha (6); and his seven-month-old daughter. His wife, Babita, was conducting prayers and religious rituals. Arvind reached home from the market. On seeing the prayers being conducted at the house, he questioned the priests. The priests informed him that the prayers were being conducted. Arvind then began asking them for their Aadhaar cards. An argument broke out between Arvind and the priests over the demand for the Aadhaar cards. Shot his wife first, then the priests According to eyewitnesses and local residents, the accused took out his licensed gun when the dispute escalated. He first shot his wife, Babita Singh. He then opened fire on both priests. People in the vicinity panicked after hearing the gunshots. After the incident, the accused, Arvind, locked himself inside the house with three children. Local people immediately informed the police. Police surrounded the house from all sides As soon as they received information about the incident, SP Dr Anil Kumar, SP Rural Chirag Jain and forces from three police stations reached the spot. After the incident, the police who arrived at the scene surrounded the house from all sides. The officers reached the spot and were engaged in efforts to safely bring the children out of the house. According to preliminary information, all three people died after being shot. However, the police said that the deaths and the reasons behind the incident would be officially confirmed only after the investigation was completed. The police took control of the scene and began collecting evidence. There is an atmosphere of fear in the village and surrounding areas following the incident. A large number of villagers have gathered at the spot. Police are investigating the entire matter and trying to determine the reason behind the incident.
