stories.title: Gorakhpur municipal commissioner rebukes officials:Expresses displeasure over sanitation in Ward 35; supervisor’s salary withheld
stories.summary: Municipal Commissioner Ajay Jain inspected Ward 35, Jungle Salik Ram, on Friday and reviewed ongoing construction, drainage, sanitation and door-to-door waste collection. He expressed displeasure over the condition of sanitation and waste-lifting arrangements and directed that the salary of sanitation supervisor Mohammad Idris be withheld until further orders. Councillor Sudhir Yadav, the executive engineer, assistant engineers from the construction and waterworks departments, the zonal officer, sanitation inspector and other officials were present during the inspection. Drain construction inspected, engineers asked to speed up work Jain inspected drainage construction at several locations and checked the depth and quality of the work. He directed engineers to speed up the construction while ensuring compliance with prescribed quality standards. He also inspected the drain near the Nishad Party office and directed the PWD engineer to take immediate steps for its repair. Roads and parks to be developed as per local requirements The Municipal Commissioner directed officials to construct roads in parks and other locations where required. He also asked Construction Division-2 to complete patchwork in the Shatabdipuram area at the earliest. He ordered the immediate removal of shuttering material, construction materials and debris lying near the drains. He also stressed regular drain cleaning to prevent blockages and waterlogging during the rains. Old Padri Bazar toilet to be developed as aspirational toilet Jain directed officials to develop the old toilet at the Padri Bazar intersection as an aspirational toilet according to local requirements. He also instructed officials to take steps to beautify the nearby pond and repair parks in the surrounding area. Door-to-door waste collection system found unsatisfactory The Municipal Commissioner expressed displeasure over the door-to-door waste collection system and ordered officials to inspect the registers of waste collection vehicle drivers. He directed all waste collection vehicles to reach the ward on time, make two to three trips and transport the collected waste to the GTS. He also stressed the need to improve revenue collection along with waste management. Sanitation supervisor’s salary withheld over poor arrangements Jain found the ward’s sanitation arrangements unsatisfactory and held the concerned staff responsible for the lapses. He directed that sanitation supervisor Mohammad Idris’s salary be withheld until further orders. He also ordered officials to verify the attendance of sanitation workers and improve the system after finding that garbage collection vehicles were not reaching the ward on time. Officials told to complete public works within deadline Jain instructed officials to ensure there was no negligence in sanitation, drainage or construction work. He directed them to prioritise public amenities, complete projects within the stipulated time and maintain the required quality standards.

stories.title: Sampurnanand Sanskrit University gate work incomplete for 6 months:₹78 lakh project includes 2 gates; eastern gate to be ready in 2 months
stories.summary: The eastern gate of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University is expected to be completed within the next two months. The university is constructing two new gates, eastern and southern, at a total cost of ₹78 lakh. Construction of the eastern gate has been underway for around six months but is yet to be completed. The university administration has now set a target to finish the work within the next two months. Construction of the southern gate will begin after the eastern gate is completed. Eastern gate construction underway for six months University engineer Ram Vijay Singh said, “₹78 lakh has been allocated for the construction of both gates. The eastern gate is currently being constructed, while work on the southern gate will begin later.” He added, “The construction of the eastern gate is slightly behind schedule and is now expected to be completed within two months.” Work on second gate to begin after first is completed University engineer Ram Vijay Singh said construction of the second gate will begin after the gate currently under construction is completed. The university plans to complete the second gate within around two months as well. The two gates will therefore be constructed in phases, with work on the existing gate being completed first before construction of the second gate begins. Both gates to be constructed for ₹78 lakh A total budget of ₹78 lakh has been allocated for the construction of the two entrance gates. However, nearly six months have already been spent on the first gate, and the work is running behind schedule. The university administration has now set a target of completing the existing gate within the next two months. Separate tender for gate delayed construction Ram Vijay Singh said the delay was partly due to the work being tendered separately. The agency was first awarded the contract to construct the boundary wall, while a separate tender was later issued for the gate. As a result, gate construction started only after the boundary wall work was completed. Singh said the gate could have been completed along with the boundary wall if both works had been tendered together.

stories.title: Bar Association election ballot boxes looted in Sultanpur:High Court assigns District Judge task of identifying accused; SP to supervise probe
stories.summary: The Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court has directed the Sultanpur district judge to identify lawyers seen in CCTV footage in connection with the alleged looting of ballot boxes during the Sultanpur District Bar Association election. The court termed the incident a criminal act and contempt of court. Ballot boxes taken away during counting The election was held peacefully on September 9. However, during vote counting on September 10, a group of lawyers allegedly took away the ballot boxes, forcing the counting process to stop. The following day, the lock of the room where the ballot boxes were kept was broken. The CCTV digital video recorder and footage were allegedly tampered with. An FIR was registered on September 14 in connection with the incident. District judge asked to conduct inquiry The High Court directed the district judge to conduct an inquiry with the assistance of the Elders Committee and submit a report after identifying the lawyers involved through CCTV footage. The Sultanpur SP has been directed to supervise the investigation into the FIR. Court orders fresh election The High Court also directed that the District Bar Association election be held afresh. The next hearing in the matter has been scheduled for October 22.

stories.title: Major accident on Agra-Lucknow Expressway:Speeding car overturns, 3 killed; 2 critically injured
stories.summary: A major road accident took place on the Agra-Lucknow Expressway on Saturday morning. A speeding car lost control and overturned near Bajidpur in the Dauki police station area. Three people travelling in the car died at the spot, while two others were seriously injured. Five people were travelling to Ballia According to reports, five people were travelling in the car from Delhi to Ballia. The vehicle suddenly went out of control near Bajidpur and overturned at high speed. The accident was so severe that three occupants died at the spot. Police investigating the accident Police reached the spot after receiving information about the accident. The injured were taken to hospital for treatment, where their condition is reported to be serious. Police took custody of the bodies and sent them for post-mortem examination. Officials are investigating the cause of the accident. The incident briefly created panic at the spot.

stories.title: 591 vials of fake anti-rabies vaccine found in Kanpur:Same batch stock as Delhi recovered; samples sent to Himachal lab
stories.summary: The investigation into drug agencies sealed in Kanpur following the seizure of fake anti-rabies vaccines in Delhi continued until late Friday night. The Drug Department team examined the stock and purchase and sales records at New RJ Firm on Birhana Road. During the investigation, officials found 591 vials from the same batch of fake Abhayrab vaccine that was seized in Delhi. The department has confiscated all the recovered vials and sent samples to a laboratory in Himachal Pradesh for testing. Examination of the records has also indicated that the vaccine may have been supplied to other states apart from Kanpur. Officials are now tracing the destinations and quantities of the consignments. Two agencies sealed following Delhi input Drug Inspector Ompal Singh said information about Kanpur-based New RJ and Alexure firms emerged after fake anti-rabies vaccines were found at Bhagirath Palace in Delhi’s Chandni Chowk. Based on the information, two drug establishments, including the agencies on Birhana Road, were sealed on Wednesday. On Friday, officials examined New RJ’s stock and purchase and sales records in the presence of the firm’s operator. Related stock received on September 18 The investigation found that New RJ received stock of the vaccine from the relevant batch on September 18. The Drug Department is now trying to determine the source of the consignment, the quantity supplied to the firm and where the vaccines were sent afterwards. The firm operator’s statement is also being recorded. Officials are using the records to trace the vaccine’s entire supply chain. Vaccine may have been supplied to other states According to officials, examination of the records has found evidence that the vaccine was supplied outside Kanpur as well. Officials are identifying the locations where the consignments were sent and matching the quantities supplied to each location with the available records. No fake stock found at Alexure Ompal Singh said the investigation of Alexure is also underway. No stock of fake vaccine has been found there so far. Further action will be decided after the documents and available stock at both agencies have been examined.

stories.title: Chitrakoot braces for second wave of floods in 26 days:Mandakini rises above danger mark; MP, UP on alert, deploy SDRF
stories.summary: Mandakini River is once again in spate due to continuous rain in the hilly areas of Chitrakoot in Satna. On Friday evening, the river's water level crossed the danger mark at Ramghat in Uttar Pradesh. Water began reaching the steps of the ghat and the surrounding low-lying areas. As the water level rose, shopkeepers began moving their goods to safer locations. On the Madhya Pradesh side, the Mandakini's water level near Arogyadham was recorded at 135.02 metres at 8 p.m. on 25 September. This is 4.58 metres below the maximum flood level of 139.60 metres. As the water level continues to rise, the administration has stepped up monitoring. See four pictures of the Mandakini River... Water crosses danger mark at Ramghat As the water level rose on Friday evening, the Mandakini reached the steps of the ghat at Ramghat. The situation also began to worsen as water accumulated in the surrounding low-lying areas. Seeing the rising water level, several shopkeepers vacated their shops and moved essential goods to safer places. The rising water also affected the movement of devotees and local residents at Ramghat. The administration has urged people to avoid going to the river and the lower areas of the ghat. Water level rises rapidly as darkness sets in After dusk, the water level of the Mandakini appeared to be rising rapidly. People in the Ramghat area became increasingly concerned upon seeing the water move towards the ghat steps. People living along the riverbank and in low-lying areas have been asked to remain alert. Flood-like conditions develop for the second time in 26 days Flood-like conditions have developed in the Mandakini for the second time within 26 days. Before this, the river's water level had also reached a dangerous level on 29 and 30 August. During that period, people were trapped in the floods in several areas, including Ramghat. The Air Force had to be called in for the rescue operation. This time too, the Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh administrations are on alert after the water level rose. SDRF deployed in Chitrakoot, administration steps up monitoring Collector Dr Satish Kumar S and SP Hansraj Singh reached Chitrakoot on Friday evening. They reviewed the flood situation with officials. Officials have been instructed to remain alert and, if necessary, move people living in low-lying areas to safe places and shelters. An SDRF team has been deployed in Chitrakoot. Announcements are being made in areas along the river to alert people. Collector Dr. Satish Kumar S said the Mandakini's water level was being monitored continuously. If necessary, people affected by the floods would be moved to safe locations. Administration appeals to people to stay away from the River and Ghats The administration has appealed to people not to go to the river or the lower sections of the ghats. stories.title: Daily festival special train to run between Gorakhpur-Pune:4 trains affected on Gonda route; check full schedule
stories.summary: To meet the increased demand for travel during the festive season, the Railways will operate a festival special train between Gorakhpur and Pune. Train Nos. 01415/01416 will run between Hadapsar-Pune and Gorakhpur from October 16 to November 17. The service will make a total of 32 trips in both directions and will have 18 coaches. Meanwhile, the operation of four trains on the Gorakhpur-Gonda section will be changed on September 26 and 27 due to ongoing automatic signalling work. Trains running from Prayagraj Sangam to Mankapur and Basti will operate only up to Ayodhya Cantt, with services beyond Ayodhya Cantt cancelled on the affected sections. Daily train from Pune to Gorakhpur from October 16 The 01415 Hadapsar-Pune-Gorakhpur Festival Special will run daily from October 16 to November 16. The train will depart from Hadapsar at 7:05 am and reach Gorakhpur at 4 am on the third day. It will halt at Daund Chord Line, Ahilyanagar, Belapur, Kopargaon, Manmad, Bhusaval, Khandwa, Itarsi, Bhopal, Bina, Virangana Lakshmibai Jhansi, Orai, Kanpur Central, Lucknow, Gonda, Mankapur and Basti. Gorakhpur train to depart at 5:30 pm The 01416 Gorakhpur-Hadapsar Festival Special will run daily from October 17 to November 17. It will depart from Gorakhpur at 5:30 pm and travel via Basti, Mankapur, Gonda and Lucknow. The train will reach Kanpur, Jhansi, Bina, Bhopal, Itarsi, Khandwa, Bhusaval, Manmad, Kopargaon, Belapur and Ahilyanagar the following day. It will then travel via Daund Chord Line and reach Hadapsar at 3:30 am on the third day. Festival special to have 18 coaches The train will have 18 coaches, including: Signalling work on Gorakhpur-Gonda route Automatic signalling work is underway on the 18.82-km section between Swaminarayan Chhapya, Maskanwa, Lakshmipur and Mankapur. Non-interlocking work will be carried out on September 26 and 27, leading to changes in the operation of four trains. Services of trains 14233 and 14234 changed The 14233 Prayagraj Sangam-Mankapur Express, scheduled to run on September 26, will terminate at Ayodhya Cantt instead of Mankapur. Its service between Ayodhya Cantt and Mankapur will remain cancelled. The 14234 Mankapur-Prayagraj Sangam Express, scheduled for September 27, will originate from Ayodhya Cantt instead of Mankapur. The service between Mankapur and Ayodhya Cantt will remain cancelled. Basti Express to run only up to Ayodhya Cantt The 14231 Prayagraj Sangam-Basti Express scheduled for September 26 will terminate at Ayodhya Cantt instead of Basti. Its onward service to Basti will remain cancelled. The 14232 Basti-Prayagraj Sangam Express, also scheduled for September 26, will originate from Ayodhya Cantt instead of Basti. It will not operate between Basti and Ayodhya Cantt. The Railways has advised passengers to check the revised train schedules before travelling on September 26 and 27.

stories.title: Officials appointed for Gorakhpur teachers’ MLC election:DM assigns nodal officers, with duties fixed from polling through vote counting and other poll arrangements
stories.summary: Officials have been appointed in Gorakhpur to oversee the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council election for the Gorakhpur-Faizabad Teachers’ Constituency. District Magistrate Deepak Meena on Friday appointed nodal, in-charge and assistant in-charge officers for various election-related responsibilities. They will be responsible for ensuring that the election is conducted freely and fairly. Duties assigned for polling arrangements Chief Development Officer Shashwat Tripurari has been given responsibility for appointing polling personnel, deploying micro-observers, sector and zonal magistrates, and conducting their training. City Magistrate Utkarsh Srivastava has been appointed nodal officer for transport arrangements and preparing route charts. Settlement Officer, Consolidation Dharmendra Mishra will oversee the local printing of various election forms, as well as the packaging and distribution of stationery. Public Works Department Executive Engineer Ravi Prakash Singh has been appointed nodal officer for arrangements at the nomination and counting venues, including tents, sound and lighting systems and barricading. Law and order arrangements Additional District Magistrate (Administration) Vaibhav Sharma has been assigned responsibility for ensuring compliance with the Model Code of Conduct, maintaining peace and law and order, and resolving complaints. He will work with the City Magistrate, all Sub-Divisional Magistrates and other concerned officials. Deputy Director of Agriculture Dhananjay Singh has been assigned responsibility for arranging ballot papers and postal ballot papers, along with their packaging and distribution. Officials have also been appointed for other election-related responsibilities.

stories.title: Brajesh Pathak’s helicopter unable to take off due to rain:Storms-rain continue in UP for 50 hours, 18 killed; 3 feet waterlogged on Ganga Expressway
stories.summary: The situation is worsening in Uttar Pradesh due to heavy rain. The entire state has been witnessing intense rainfall for the past 50 hours. Strong winds are blowing at speeds of 40–50 kmph. Roads have turned into ponds, while water has entered residential colonies. The threat of flash floods looms over 32 districts. Roads have been blocked after trees and electricity poles were uprooted. So far, 18 people have died. In Varanasi, Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak’s helicopter could not take off due to bad weather. He eventually had to travel to Ghazipur by road. In Unnao, water up to 3 feet deep has accumulated on a 500-metre stretch of the Ganga Expressway. The state received 52.5 mm of rain in the past 24 hours, 25 times the normal 2.7 mm. In percentage terms, this is more than 1,800% above normal. The state has also received its full monsoon rainfall quota for the season. Since June 1, Uttar Pradesh has recorded 751.9 mm of rain, 2% above the normal quota of 738 mm for this period. Due to heavy rainfall, instant home delivery services in Lucknow and Gorakhpur have slowed down for some time. In several areas, platforms such as Zomato, Blinkit and Zepto are showing ‘delivery unavailable’. In Chitrakoot, the Mandakini river is flowing above the danger mark. The DM and SP are making announcements warning that the water level is rising and asking shopkeepers to close their shops and return home. In Lucknow, water has entered homes, reaching kitchens and bedrooms. Several lanes are flooded up to waist level. In Bareilly and Fatehpur, 2–3 feet of water has accumulated in streets and neighbourhoods. CM Yogi has urged people not to step out unnecessarily and to take care of their loved ones. He said the government stands with the people. See pictures of the rain and flooding…

stories.title: What will Divya Mittal do after quitting IAS:Job, business or coaching?; Says, ‘I’m enjoying a break for now…’
stories.summary: Former Uttar Pradesh IAS officer Divya Mittal is now set to begin a new chapter in her life. She submitted her resignation on 30 August, which the state government accepted on 14 September. Having built a reputation through her work, her millions of followers are now keen to know what she plans to do next. Divya Mittal told Dainik Bhaskar about her career plans, resignation and future plans. Read the full report… Divya said ‘I am giving time to myself ’ Divya Mittal says she has taken a month-long break. She has travelled outside Uttar Pradesh and wants to spend some time in peace. She says she is reflecting on her journey so far and on the life ahead. She is not thinking too much at the moment and wants to do whatever feels right to her. Asked about her plans for the future — whether she would take up a job or start a business, Divya said, “I have not yet decided whether I will take up a job or start a business. But whatever decision I make, I will inform my supporters myself.” Resignation accepted; Divya visits Mata Vaishno Devi temple Divya Mittal’s administrative career has remained completely unblemished. This is why there were no hurdles in the process of accepting her resignation. The Uttar Pradesh government accepted it on 14 September. Even before her resignation was formally accepted, Divya had travelled to Katra in Jammu on 12 September to seek the blessings of Mata Vaishno Devi. She was seen without any fanfare — wearing red clothes, sunglasses and carrying a stick. She was seen walking towards the temple with other people in a very simple manner. After offering prayers at the temple, she posted a video on social media with an emotional caption. She wrote, “Mother, you have given me everything without me asking… but the road ahead is difficult. Give me the wisdom to understand what is right and what is wrong.” Three possibilities being discussed — will she teach IAS aspirants or join a business?

stories.title: One home, crores in business and broken relationships... then murder:Son had father killed after growing resentment over his lavish lifestyle; 5 characters
stories.summary: The story of the murder of Kanpur millionaire pharma businessman Vineet Minocha is chilling. Years of conflict within a wealthy family, growing distance between father and son, financial difficulties and layers of mistrust have come to light. Vineet's son Subrat's resentment towards his father deepened when his mother Punita decided to separate from her husband and live with their daughter. Vineet had also begun openly talking at home about his indulgence and extramarital relationships. The growing tension in the family eventually culminated in a murder conspiracy. When police investigated the case, five key characters emerged. First was pharma businessman Vineet Minocha, who ran a business worth crores of rupees in Kanpur. Second was his son and the main accused in the murder, Subrat. Third was his daughter-in-law, Shalu, whose relationship with Subrat was also a source of suspicion towards his father. Fourth was servant Vishal Gautam, who allegedly accepted a contract from Subrat to kill Vineet. Fifth was Subrat's mother, Punita, who was troubled by her husband's alleged indulgence. According to her son, she had told him, “Do something about him (Vineet).” Where did the rift between father and son begin, how did it grow, what role did debt and family tensions play, and how was the murder conspiracy eventually planned? Read Dainik Bhaskar's special report. Vineet Minocha owned Pharma Traders in Kanpur's Birhana Road medicine market. He was a wholesaler and retailer of medicines. Twenty-three people worked at his shop, which had an annual turnover of around ₹50-60 crore. Vineet lived with his son Subrat, daughter-in-law Shalu and grandson Shrijay in a luxury flat at the upscale Ratan Orbit society in Kanpur's Indira Nagar. Relations between pharma businessman Vineet and his wife Punita were not good. Subrat had also told the media that his mother decided to separate from his father because of his alleged indulgence. Punita had subsequently been living with her daughter Shubhangi, who lives in Gurugram, for the past seven years. After his mother separated from his father, Subrat's resentment towards Vineet deepened for the first time, as he believed his father's behaviour had forced his mother to leave. This is where his hatred towards his father began to grow. The main accused in the murder case is Vineet's son Subrat. Subrat studied up to Class 8 at different schools in Kanpur. He then completed his intermediate education and pursued higher studies in Nainital. Subrat married Shalu, a resident of Lucknow's Thakurganj, in 2020. Subrat suspected that his father had inappropriate intentions towards his wife. On one occasion, Vineet's hand accidentally touched Shalu's body inside a car, which angered Subrat. However, during police questioning, Shalu said that he had not touched her inappropriately and that his hand had accidentally made contact with her. She said he had never behaved improperly or harassed her. Shalu is originally from Thakurganj in Lucknow. She also comes from a prominent pharma business family. She had an arranged marriage with Subrat in 2020. After the marriage, not only Subrat but also Shalu became frustrated with her father-in-law's restrictions and interference. As a result, Shalu frequently argued with Vineet. Vineet had also installed cameras at home to monitor his son and daughter-in-law, which further troubled Shalu and Subrat. Vishal Gautam, who lived in a slum area of the Rail Bazaar locality, came from a very poor family. He lives with his younger brother and mother, while his father lives separately and has no contact with the family. Vishal was also carrying a debt of several lakh rupees. He had worked at Vineet Minocha's medical store from 2010 to 2022, but Vineet dismissed him over theft. Subrat himself had allegedly arranged the theft for which Vishal was dismissed. This created sympathy between Subrat and Vishal, and both Shalu and Subrat would call Vishal to do household work. This angered Vineet towards his son. How did the son become his father's killer? Spent lakhs on indulgence but gave his son only ₹40,000 Vineet Minocha's alleged indulgence led his wife Punita to decide to live separately from him in 2019. She subsequently moved to Gurugram to live with her daughter and son-in-law. According to Subrat, after his wife left him, Vineet's indulgence increased further. There was no longer anyone to stop or question him. Subrat, Vineet's only son, gradually developed deep resentment towards his father. He said his father frequently travelled to Goa and Mumbai with different women. He also had close relationships with several women in the city. He allegedly spent lakhs of rupees on his lifestyle, but despite being married and having a son, he gave Subrat only ₹40,000 a month for expenses. To meet his expenses, Subrat even had to steal from the shop. After completing his studies in Nainital, he began handling his father's business, but only as an employee. He did not have ownership rights over anything. ₹40 lakh debt increased son's stress The police investigation found that Subrat was fond of attending high-end parties, gambling and had also become addicted to drugs. His expenses could not be covered with ₹40,000. He was caught stealing several times, after which his father became strict with him. Vineet would often threaten to disinherit Subrat if he opposed him or drank alcohol. Subrat took loans from five different sources to fund his and his wife's lifestyle. He then took further loans to repay the earlier ones, eventually accumulating a debt of around ₹40 lakh. While the debt caused him mental stress, his father's strictness further pushed him into distress. Father allegedly killed for ₹6 lakh contract Three months ago, Subrat began planning the murder with Vishal Gautam, a worker who had left the shop. They initially planned to kill Vineet in an accident, but the plan did not work. They then planned to hire contract killers, but Vishal could not find anyone willing to carry out the murder. Vishal then allegedly took the contract himself, along with his friend Rajkishore, for ₹6 lakh. Vineet was stabbed to death on the night of September 5. Vishal and his friend then fled the scene. Mother-in-law and daughter-in-law don't get along, what happens to the business now? Vineet Minocha was among Kanpur's top five pharma businessmen. His annual turnover was more than ₹60 crore, and he also owned property worth crores of rupees. Vineet had prepared a will regarding his property, so there is unlikely to be a dispute over its distribution. However, the business could become a point of contention between his wife and daughter-in-law. Since Subrat was sent to jail, his mother, Punita, is currently in possession of the Ratan Orbit flat and the business. However, Shalu could stake a claim to the property after coming out of jail. According to family members, the relationship between the mother-in-law and daughter-in-law is extremely strained. Only after Shalu comes out will it become clear who will take charge of the business. Mother's return could end son's distress Following Vineet's murder and Shalu's arrest, their five-year-old son has been staying with his maternal grandmother in Lucknow. With both his mother and now his father in jail, he has been left virtually alone. He keeps asking to speak to his parents over the phone and video calls throughout the day. His maternal family is extremely worried about him. For this reason, Shalu's family had begun pursuing her release through the court after she was sent to jail. However, following the remand and the developments in the case, the police investigation has raised questions about Shalu's involvement. Her family now hopes she can be released from jail. Family members are in constant contact with the officers investigating the case and the police, hoping that the police will soon submit their report and Shalu will be released. Crores in property and business, but the family has fallen apart Despite having so much wealth, the family has been torn apart by conflict. Vineet was murdered, his only son Subrat went to jail, and Shalu may now be released, but she is unlikely to live with her mother-in-law because of their strained relationship. Neither Shalu nor Vineet's wife Punita had ever managed the business. The entire business has also remained shut for the past 25 days. The market is owed crores of rupees. If the situation continues, matters could become even more difficult in the coming days. Meanwhile, the 23 employees who worked at the shop have also begun taking jobs elsewhere because they are facing uncertainty over their livelihoods. As a result, there is now no one left to manage the business.

stories.title: Degree colleges built in UP forests and fields:No proper road access; no regular classes, students come only to sit exams
stories.summary: Several private degree colleges in Uttar Pradesh have been opened in forests and deserted areas. Some do not even have proper roads leading to them. This has allegedly been done so that officials cannot reach the colleges for inspections. Universities have also granted them affiliation without proper scrutiny. These colleges are operating with little oversight. Classes are not held throughout the year, and students come only to appear for exams. College authorities allow students to cheat during exams. Attracted by this, students from distant areas are taking admission to these colleges. Dainik Bhaskar investigated how these colleges were allowed to open in such locations, what their condition is and how they are charging two to three times the prescribed fee while allegedly guaranteeing that students will pass. We used hidden cameras to record principals, teachers and managers at colleges in three districts while they negotiated the sale of degrees. We also found these major irregularities- These colleges in Auraiya, Farrukhabad and Etah offer courses ranging from BA and BSc to BEd and BTC. Read the full investigation... College amid fields in Auraiya — classes closed, not a single student present... Shri Krishna Saroj Mahavidyalaya is located in Kakore, around 20 km from the Auraiya district headquarters. There is no proper paved road from the main highway to the college. After travelling around 500 metres, a building appeared amid the fields. The classrooms were locked and there were no students on the premises. The college has affiliation from Chhatrapati Shahu Ji Maharaj University for BA, BSc, BEd and BTC courses. On paper, 18 teachers and 678 students are registered here. We met the principal, Dr Anil Kumar Tiwari. When we began speaking to him using a hidden camera, the reality of the college came to light. Reporter: When did the college open and which university is it affiliated with? Principal: It has been running since 2014. It has affiliation from Chhatrapati Shahu Ji Maharaj University, Kanpur, for BA, BSc, BEd and BTC. Reporter: There is no road to the college? Principal: Gravel was laid here earlier. But because of objections from local people, the road could not be built. Reporter: How many students and teachers are there? Principal: There are currently 678 students and 18 teachers. Including the other staff, there are around 30 people. Around 12 of them come from Kanpur and travel back and forth every day. Most of them teach BEd and BTC. They should be kept here until 3 pm. But they say, ‘Sir, let us leave,’ and we tell them to go. The only thing is that classes should not be disturbed. Reporter: So are classes held regularly? Principal: Nobody comes regularly. Around 10-20% of students attend D.El.Ed and BEd. No one comes for BSc. Reporter: Why does this happen? Principal: I hesitate to say it, but now we have to allow cheating. If we do not, we will fall behind. There will be no admissions. There is another college here. It has four times as many students as us. In exams, anyone can sit in place of any student. So this has become the entire system here. Reporter: What is the admission process? Principal: The admission process is the same whether it is a government or private college. You have to register on the university website. The fee is ₹300. After that, you can take admission in any college. Reporter: Private colleges ask for documents on WhatsApp. Is admission done on that basis? Principal: We do that too. We have students from as far as Hardoi. They sent their documents, we submitted them to the office and the admission was done. The money also comes online. Reporter: How much is the fee? Principal: The actual fee is ₹1,800. But as a college, we are charging ₹6,000. Another college is charging ₹12,000. The surprising thing is that even after charging ₹6,000, we have only 600 admissions. Despite charging ₹12,000, they have 1,700 admissions. The only reason is that the college provides students with complete facilities. Even if they fail, they get them passed by going to the university. Now, students will go wherever they get more facilities. Everyone gets a scholarship. We only have to send the list to the Social Welfare Department. Reporter: Can a student even come top? Is that possible? Principal: Earlier, we used to prepare practical files throughout the night. Now, students do not even know what a practical is. Reporter: So does this happen everywhere? Principal: Yes, it happens like this, but not in every college. Some colleges still maintain their reputation. But they have become less than 1%. Reporter: Is there also a rule that there should be separate buildings for the number of courses being run? Principal: Yes, there is such a rule. Reporter: But you are running so many courses from a single building? Principal: If you go by the rules, the rules are very strict. Reporter: So what system do you work under? Principal: One system overrides every other system. The same system works everywhere. Actually, our BA and BSc courses are affiliated with Kanpur University, while we have taken affiliation for BEd from Allahabad University. The two universities have different websites, so the game works. College manager’s offer — no need to attend classes, only come to sit the exams Around 3 km from the Kanpur-Etawah Highway, Suman Rani Institute of Technology was found amid fields in Bamuripur, Auraiya. There is an unpaved road leading to the college. By the time we arrived, manager Ram Sagar Dwivedi and the clerk had closed the college and left. They said it had been closed before 4 pm because there were no students. Staff said 16 teachers and around 500 students are registered there. Reporter: We live in Lucknow. The family lives here. Our daughter is preparing for NEET and we want to get her admitted. Manager: The site is closed everywhere at the moment. Send us the documents and we will get the form filled in. Reporter: So will she need to come here? Manager: No, there will be no need to come. She will only have to come to sit the exams. Reporter: Will she have to come for practicals as well? Manager: Practicals are done anyway. But if there is a need, you will have to call us. Otherwise, it gets done. Reporter: How will the admission be done? Manager: Just send the documents. It will be done. Reporter: How much is the fee? Will everything be included or will there be additional charges? Manager: The fee is ₹3,500. Apart from this, the university conducts a paper on AI and cyber-related subjects. The university charges ₹500 for that. That will be charged when the paper takes place. Everything else will be taken care of. College in Farrukhabad surrounded by water; staff says — forget the prospectus, take admission directly After travelling around 130 km from Auraiya, we reached Farrukhabad. At Amritpur on the Bareilly-Delhi Highway, we found Virendra Singh Katiyar Mahavidyalaya. The college was surrounded by water on all sides. We met an employee, Satish Singh, who agreed to show us around the college in connection with admission. The classrooms in the basement were found submerged in water. Classroom equipment had been moved to the first floor. The college is affiliated with Chhatrapati Shahu Ji Maharaj University, Kanpur. On paper, 200 students and around 10 teachers are shown as registered. Reporter: Will someone be available at the college? We wanted to make admission. Employee: No one... tell me. Is it BSc, BEd or BTC? Reporter: We want admission in BSc. Employee: It will be done. Reporter: We live in Lucknow. We want to get our daughter admitted. She lives here. Employee: Then send the documents on WhatsApp. It will be done. Reporter: Do you have a prospectus for the college? Employee: What will you do with a prospectus? You will just need four photographs, a photocopy of the Aadhaar card, email ID, photocopies of the High School and Intermediate mark sheets, and a mobile number. Reporter: Will she have to travel here every day? Employee: No, she does not have to come every day. Reporter: When will she have to come, then? Employee: She will be called when she has to sit an exam, when there is a practical or if there is any problem. Reporter: What will the fee be? Employee: The fee is ₹4,000 per semester. The practical is separate. You tell us in advance because our centre is assigned separately. We personally deposit the money for every student there, for the cheating facility. Reporter: The child will not fail, will she? Employee: We cannot guarantee that. If the student keeps writing — meaning their hand keeps moving on the paper — they will not fail. Reporter: But if the student does not even come, how will they study? Employee: Get a notebook for them. Even if they do not come, there is no problem. Reporter: Does teaching take place here? Employee: Yes, students who want to come can study. Reporter: So you have teachers here? Employee: There are 10 teachers. Reporter: How many students are there? Employee: The students do not come at all. Reporter: Even then, how many students are enrolled? Employee: We have capacity for 240 students. At present, there are 200 students. Reporter: You are saying the student may or may not come. But attendance must also be required? Employee: We have to submit 75% attendance for every student. We have no choice; we have to manage it. Reporter: What is your principal’s name? Employee: In a government college, the principal is a gazetted officer. Our principal lives in Farrukhabad itself. His name is Pushpendra Gangwar. Reporter: Does he not come? Employee: No... he does come. Reporter: Is it possible for a student to get a first division or 75% marks? Would that require any additional payment? Employee: No, there is no additional payment. The student just has to keep writing. All facilities will be provided to the student. Reporter: Does cheating happen? Employee: Yes, that is what I am telling you. We have a setting. Their students come to us and our students go to them. Reporter: So the exam centre is at another college? Employee: Our Ram Niwas Degree College is right next to us. Reporter: Which university are you affiliated with? Employee: Kanpur. Reporter: Is that facility only for practicals or for everything? Employee: No, it is for everything. The student will not face any problem; they will pass. Reporter: Can the marks not be increased? Employee: Not just marks... our students score up to 85%. Muddy road to Etah college; reporter’s feet got stuck Around 115 km from Farrukhabad, we found a college built in a deserted area in Sarai Aghat, Etah. There is no proper road leading to Lala Ram Ladaite Ram Shri Devi Mahavidyalaya. Despite several attempts, our car could not go any further, even though the college was only 500 metres from the main road. We then hired a local motorbike. Even then, our feet got stuck in a pothole. We eventually entered the college on the pretext of washing our feet. There, we met a man named Brijendra Singh, who said he was a teacher. The college appeared to have been closed for several weeks. It is affiliated with Raja Mahendra Pratap Singh State University in Aligarh. Reporter: Whose college is this? Teacher: It belongs to Master Umesh. He also has an Intermediate college on Aliganj Road. Reporter: What is taught here? Are admissions taking place? Teacher: BA and BSc are offered here. Admissions are taking place. Reporter: Can we get an admission form? Teacher: Bring the documents. It will be done. High School and Intermediate mark sheets and Aadhaar card. Reporter: Do students have to come and go here? Teacher: If the students want to come, they can. Otherwise, get them admitted. Then bring the student when there is an exam or practical. Reporter: How much is the BSc fee? Teacher: ₹3,500 per semester, ₹7,000 for one year. Reporter: Do students pass? Teacher: Yes, we give the practical marks ourselves. Teachers come from outside, but it gets managed. Do not worry about the marks; we will get good marks for them. Reporter: Is there any separate fee for that? Teacher: No, there is no separate fee. Reporter: If we pay more, can the student get a better rank? Teacher: It will cost ₹7,000 for one year. Everything will be done within that. Reporter: Will the child come first? Teacher: There is no problem. Aligarh University is better than Kanpur. Reporter: If we pay ₹3,500, is it the college’s responsibility? Teacher: Everything is included in this. Reporter: Can the fee for all semesters be deposited together, or how does it work? Teacher: Keep paying the fee as each semester comes. Reporter: How will she write her exam paper, then? Teacher: Everything will be taken care of. No, you will not have to pay anything extra. Many students do not come at all. The examiners who come simply enter the marks. Etah college gate locked; overgrown bushes suggest it has not opened for days Shri Hiralal Memorial Mahavidyalaya is located in Naktai Khurd in Etah’s Aliganj tehsil. For around 500 metres, the road looks as though you are travelling through a forest. The college gate was locked. There were large bushes across the ground. The college appeared not to have opened for several days. Even after waiting for some time, no one came to the college. It is affiliated with Raja Mahendra Pratap Singh State University in Aligarh. Around 12 teachers and 650 students are registered here. Colleges taking advantage of relaxed rules Question: How are these colleges allowed to open in deserted areas? Why is there no monitoring? Answer: The government believes that everyone should have access to higher education, so the rules are relaxed. Colleges take advantage of this. Before granting affiliation to a college, a committee visits the premises and checks whether the required standards have been met. Once affiliation is granted, there are no further visits. If a complaint is received against a college, the university forms a new panel. Only then can an inspection take place. Question: How much funding do these colleges receive and from whom? Answer: In most universities in Uttar Pradesh, the fee for BA or BSc is ₹1,000 to ₹1,200 per semester, or ₹2,400 a year. Colleges add up to 80% in tuition fees and charge ₹6,000 to ₹7,000 a year. A fixed charge was also collected from all students before examinations. This makes it a substantial amount. Question: Then how do these colleges make money? Answer: Suppose the fee for a course is ₹4,000 and 300 students are enrolled in the college. That means the college receives ₹12 lakh per semester from one course. Even after deducting the university fee, teachers’ salaries and other expenses, ₹8 lakh remains per semester. Question: Then why do students take admission in such colleges? Answer: There are three types of students who reach such colleges: Students who live away from home and do small jobs. They take admission in such colleges to obtain a degree. In many parts of Uttar Pradesh, families still do not send girls far away from home. Such families enrol their daughters in these colleges so that they do not have to attend classes every day. Students pursuing professional courses take admission in these colleges for dummy courses. However, such students account for only 10-15%. (The answers to these questions are based on a conversation with Professor Dr VK Katiyar, general secretary of the Kanpur University Principals’ Association.)

stories.title: UCC unlikely before UP Assembly polls:BJP wary of risk; fears Muslim voters could fully shift towards SP
stories.summary: The Uniform Civil Code (UCC) is unlikely to be implemented in Uttar Pradesh before the 2027 Assembly elections, as no formal drafting exercise has reportedly begun in the state. Union Home Minister Amit Shah said on September 13 that the UCC would be implemented in all 21 BJP-led NDA states before the 2029 Lok Sabha elections, while reports from Uttar Pradesh indicate that the process has yet to begin. The political debate over the timing of UCC has intensified ahead of the UP elections. BJP leaders and political observers have discussed whether introducing the law before the state polls could affect the electoral contest. The 2027 Assembly elections are expected in February-March. Why UCC may not be implemented in UP before the elections, explained in 8 points… 1. Long process and little time before elections: A drafting committee would first have to be formed to prepare the UCC framework. Public consultation would then be required before a report and legislation could be prepared. The Bill would subsequently have to go through the legislative process and, if required, receive presidential assent. The timeline for such a process can be lengthy. With the UP Assembly elections expected in early 2027, completing all these stages before the polls could be difficult. Uttarakhand's experience also shows that the process does not end with passage of a Bill. Its UCC was implemented in January 2025, after the President's approval, and detailed rules were subsequently prepared. 2. No precise assessment of political gains or losses: There is no publicly available survey establishing what the electoral impact of implementing the UCC immediately before the UP elections would be. The possible political consequences therefore remain a matter of speculation and competing assessments. 3. Possibility of consolidation among Muslim voters: One argument being discussed in political circles is that introducing the UCC before the election could consolidate Muslim voters behind the Samajwadi Party. At the same time, other parties such as the BSP and AIMIM are seeking space among different sections of the electorate. Such assessments are political projections rather than established electoral outcomes. Recent reporting has also noted that UP's political contest has involved competing attempts to consolidate different caste and community groups. 4. BJP already has support from upper and backward-caste allies: The BJP's NDA alliance in Uttar Pradesh includes parties such as the Rashtriya Lok Dal, Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party, Nishad Party and Apna Dal (S). Their social bases include sections of backward and extremely backward communities. The BJP may therefore continue to focus on its existing alliance and social coalition rather than immediately making UCC the central issue of the state election. The positions of some allies on UCC, however, have remained cautious and not all have publicly endorsed a specific draft. 5. Impact of implementation in other states will be watched: The experience of states that have already introduced or passed UCC legislation is likely to provide information on implementation, public response and legal challenges. Uttarakhand became the first state to implement a state-specific UCC in January 2025. Bills passed in Assam, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh were still awaiting presidential assent as of September 2026. 6. A major issue could be kept for 2029: Amit Shah has explicitly set a pre-2029 target for implementing UCC across all NDA-ruled states. This has led to speculation that the larger rollout could be aligned with the period before the next Lok Sabha election rather than necessarily being completed in every state before its next Assembly election. 7. State initiative could follow a central framework: One issue under discussion is whether the Centre should first bring forward a national framework before states such as Uttar Pradesh adopt their own legislation. However, a national UCC Bill for all states has not been announced as a specific legislative timetable. Amit Shah's September 13 statement was that NDA-ruled states would implement UCC before 2029. 8. BJP preparing to fight the election with Yogi as its face: Yogi Adityanath remains Uttar Pradesh's Chief Minister, and the BJP's current state government is preparing for the 2027 Assembly election. Recent reporting indicates that the party is making organisational preparations across the state. Any assessment of which issues will ultimately dominate the campaign remains subject to developments closer to the election. No UCC preparation currently underway in government departments Before introducing a major new law in Uttar Pradesh, the government normally involves the relevant legal and legislative departments and, where appropriate, the State Law Commission. As of September 2026, reports said the UP State Law Commission had not received a formal request to draft a UCC. Therefore, no formal drafting exercise had begun at the state level. Could a drafting committee be formed before the election? Political sources have speculated that the government could announce the formation of a drafting committee during the election period if it concludes that issues around caste are becoming more prominent in the campaign. Such a move would amount to beginning the process rather than implementing the UCC itself. Expert says UCC's impact could be significant in UP Political analyst Virendranath Bhatt said the UCC would have its most direct implications for personal-law matters such as marriage, divorce and inheritance, including those affecting Muslim communities. He said the political impact could therefore be significant in Uttar Pradesh. Amit Shah's announcement has made implementation before 2029 a stated target, but the timing of implementation remains important. 'If UCC comes, the election could become a contest between religion and caste' Senior journalist and political analyst Yogesh Shukla said that since Home Minister Amit Shah has publicly announced the 2029 target, implementation in UP before the next Lok Sabha election is expected. He also argued that if the UCC were introduced before the 2027 Assembly election, it could have a significant political effect. This is an expert's assessment, not an established electoral outcome. Understand the numbers behind UCC implementation in UP The BJP has governed Uttar Pradesh with a full majority since 2017. The party and its allies also have representation in both houses of the state legislature. However, the exact numbers and alliance arithmetic would determine whether any future UCC legislation could be passed, and presidential assent would be required for a state Bill after passage by the state legislature. Amit Shah's September 13 statement triggered speculation that the BJP could introduce the UCC in UP ahead of the 2027 Assembly election. Some political observers have argued that it could provide an alternative to the Opposition's PDA narrative, which focuses on backward, Dalit and minority communities. Other assessments point to caste-based mobilisation remaining an important feature of UP politics. At present, however, there is no formal state-level drafting exercise underway, while the publicly stated broader target is implementation across NDA-ruled states before the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.

stories.title: Two-storey house collapses after cylinder blast in Fatehpur:2 rescued from debris, several feared trapped
stories.summary: A gas cylinder exploded in a house in Fatehpur, causing a loud blast, after which part of the house collapsed. Panic spread in the area after reports that several people were trapped under the debris. Police and fire brigade teams reached the spot after receiving the information and began rescue operations. Two people injured in the incident have been admitted to a medical college. The incident occurred at around 5 p.m. on Monday in the Malwan police station area, beneath an overbridge. Search under way for people trapped in debris After the explosion, debris from the house spread across the road and surrounding area. People informed the police that some individuals were trapped under the debris. Firefighters and police personnel then began removing the debris and searching for those trapped inside. The rescue team is trying to determine how many people were inside the house when the incident occurred. The number and condition of those trapped under the debris are not clear at present. The two people injured in the incident were immediately taken to a medical college, where they are undergoing treatment. No detailed information about their condition has emerged so far. People arrived after hearing the sound of the blast According to eyewitnesses, a powerful blast suddenly occurred in the house in the evening. Within a short while, part of the house collapsed. Hearing the sound of the blast, local residents reached the spot and informed the police. A large number of people gathered at the site after the incident. The police cleared the crowd and cordoned off the scene to prevent disruption to the relief and rescue operations. The Malwan police station team and fire brigade personnel are continuously engaged in clearing the debris. Officials reached the spot and took stock of the relief and rescue operations. The police are investigating the cause of the accident and are also trying to determine how the cylinder exploded inside the house. This report is being continuously updated...

She appealed to girls to prepare themselves for self-defence and not depend on anyone. Thirty-four-year-old Khushboo advised girls to take the initiative themselves for self-defence and keep an air pistol with them. She said they should not depend on anyone for their safety. The former Army officer posted a video on Instagram on Daughters' Day (27 September), in which she can be seen firing an air pistol (Glock 17 Gen 4). She appealed to girls to undergo training in its use. Referring to Article 21 of the Constitution, Khushboo said that every person has the right to life and personal safety. She also made it clear that any means of self-defence should be used only responsibly and in serious situations. Khushboo said-What is happening in the country will never end Khushboo Patani explains that firing an air pistol does not require gunpowder or ordinary cartridges; instead, CO2 (metal pellets) is used. She has appealed to girls to visit a nearby shooting range for proper training and practice. Khushboo says, You can buy one, keep it with you and protect yourself. Do not depend on anyone. Otherwise, what is happening in India will never end. Four pictures of Khushboo Patani Girls advised to buy a 0.177 air pistol Glock 17 Gen 4 Khushboo said the air pistol costs ₹60,000-70,000. Girls can train to use it at a nearby shooting range. She also demonstrated how it works. Khushboo also added a disclaimer in the caption while sharing the video. She wrote, For self-defence only. This is not a toy, whether it is real or not. You should use it sensibly and responsibly. 0.177 air pistol Glock 17 Gen 4 for informational purposes only. Previously, too, she had shared information about self-defence Khushboo Patni had earlier also taught girls about self-defence. After shots were fired at her home in Bareilly, Khushboo Patni released a video. In it, she spoke about self-defence and safety. She had said, ‘In this Kaliyug, you never know what might happen or when. It does not matter whether you are a public figure or not.’ Khushboo had said, "If you have a licensed gun, that is fine. Otherwise, keep something for self-defence. Because anything can happen at any time." Can make a weapon from a data cable Khushboo Patani then takes a mobile phone data cable. She says, This is called a mobile data cable. Basically, we need a thick wire that will not break easily." She then takes five nets. She says, "You do not have to do anything; just insert this net inside the data cable. If you need to keep it inside a bag normally, tie five knots at both ends of the cable. It is a very powerful object-small in appearance, but capable of disfiguring the entire face. Whatever it strikes will break; if it hits the nose or the jaw, it will break them.

stories.title: Kanpur businessman murder:Court orders daughter-in-law’s immediate release; no evidence against her, son allegedly framed her after getting father killed
stories.summary: A court has ordered the immediate release of Shalu, the daughter-in-law jailed in connection with the murder of Kanpur medicine trader Vineet Minocha, ruling that she was not involved in the conspiracy to kill him. Granting her release on a personal bond of ₹50,000, the court directed, “Shalu will have to appear when summoned by the court or the investigating officer.” Following the court's order, Shalu will walk out of jail as soon as the necessary paperwork is completed. Regarding his sister's release, her brother Dheeraj Arora said, "The same police who sent her to jail found her innocent in the murder case after the investigation. The police have also filed a closure report in court." Her brother said that Shalu's son Shrijay is currently staying with him in Lucknow. After being released from jail, Shalu will not go to her in-laws' flat at Ratan Orbit in Kanpur but will travel directly to Lucknow, her parental home. Medicine businessman was murdered on 5 September Medicine businessman Vineet Minocha, a resident of flat C-104 in Indira Nagar, Ratan Orbit, was stabbed 17 times and murdered on 5 September. Last Thursday, police arrested his son, Subrat Minocha, and sent him to jail. The revelations that emerged during the police investigation were shocking. The accused son, Subrat, admitted to his crime while speaking to the media. He said his father was a womaniser and had relationships with several women. Because of this, his mother, Punita Minocha, did not live with him. He feared that, in such a situation, a woman might come to his house claiming that she was going to become the mother of Vineet's child. Subrat had confessed that he had arranged for his father's murder through his former servant, Vishal Gautam, and his accomplice, Rajkishore. Subrat, the son, said that he had told Vishal that, if he was caught, he should name Shalu. This was supported by Vishal's statement on the first day, the WhatsApp chats between the two, the voice-call details and the statement of security guard Madan Singh, who said that Shalu had told him not to record Vishal's name as Shubham and not to make an entry for him in the register. During the initial investigation, the police treated Shalu as an accused in the murder and sent her to jail. She has remained in custody since then. Subrat confessed to the crime on 24 September. The police subsequently sent him to jail. The police investigation established that Shalu was innocent, following which the police submitted a closure report in her favour in court on Friday. The court will hear the matter today, Monday. What ploy did he devise to gather evidence against his wife? DCP West S.M. Qasim Abidi says, "Subrat had hated his father, Vinit Minocha, for a long time. But he had been planning to kill him for the past one to two months. He knew that after removing his father from the way, his father's brother, Subrat's uncle Punit, would come after him. He would make every effort to find out the truth about his brother's death. A dispute could also arise over the property. "That is why he wanted to kill two birds with one stone: murder his father and frame his uncle as the killer. He told Vishal about this plan. Vishal worked at Subrat's shop and had been dismissed by Vinit seven months earlier." While planning, the two also knew that Puneet had a strong presence in the city. He would make every effort to prove his innocence. Therefore, the conspiracy was altered around 25 days earlier. Subrat then decided to portray his own wife as the mastermind of the conspiracy. To create evidence, he took his wife, Shalu, to Parade Chauraha around 20 days before the murder. Vishal met them there. The three of them went together in a car to Z Square Mall in Bada Chauraha to shop. Subrat remained seated in the car, while he sent Shalu and Vishal inside the mall to shop. This was intended to ensure that Vishal was seen with Shalu by people. When the police later checked the mobile phone locations, Shalu's location was found alongside Vishal's. Subrat then took the two of them to a Banarasi tea stall on 80 Feet Road. There, he also had a duplicate key made at Lareb's shop in Juhi Param Purwa. Subrat paid ₹100 for it through Vishal. Subrat went to a doctor to get Vishal treated. He kept his wife with him at both of the remaining locations, while he himself stayed in the car. He sent only Vishal and Shalu in front of the public. Murder night: Vineet mistook Vishal for a thief, then had to change the plan Then came the night of 5 September, when Subrat had planned to kill his father. Before the murder, Subrat called Vishal four times between 6 p.m. and 8 p.m. Vishal knew he could not carry out the task alone, so he also involved his friend Raj Kishore. As planned, Subrat left home with his wife Shalu for the party at 9:30 p.m. Before leaving, he switched off the CCTV cameras in the apartment. At 9:45 p.m., Vishal and Rajkishore entered the flat using the original key, which Subrat had already given to Vishal. The plan was that businessman Vineet usually went to sleep by around 10 p.m. every day. Subrat had told Vishal and Rajkishore to suffocate Vineet by pressing a pillow over his face. There should be no signs of a struggle in the room, so that everyone would think in the morning that he had died of a heart attack. Rajkishore and Vishal reached the businessman's room and hid there. They waited until 11:30 p.m. The businessman could not sleep and came to the room late. As soon as he switched on the light, he saw Vishal. Mistaking him for a thief, he shouted, "Help, thief... help." Vishal panicked. He had brought a knife with him and attacked Vineet with it, stabbing him 17 times. He then quickly fled the flat with Rajkishore. This was the major mistake that enabled the police to reach Vishal within just 14 hours. The two were spotted on the CCTV camera installed outside the apartment. Subrat had already prepared for this situation. As part of his plan, Vishal named Shalu before the police. Subrat had cleverly arranged for calls to be made to Vishal from Shalu's mobile phone. Without conducting a thorough investigation, Kanpur Police arrested Shalu within 24 hours and sent her to jail. Uncle said, ‘I am shocked myself-why was my nephew trying to frame her?’ As questions continued to be raised about the revelations in the case, Subrat and Vishal were confronted during their custody remand. There were so many contradictions in their conversation that it did not take the police long to realise that the two were hiding something. During questioning in a closed room, Subrat broke down and confessed to the crime. Subrat told the police that he had wanted to pin the murder on his uncle, Puneet Minocha, but could not find any solid reason to implicate him. He then had allegations made against his wife, Shalu. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to uncle Puneet Minocha. He said, "I have been living separately from my elder brother Vineet Minocha for the past 37 years. My house is in Signature City in Nawabganj. I am in the construction business. I am also baffled as to why Subrat wanted to implicate me. We rarely even met. We never had an argument, let alone a quarrel." Son said, ‘I am glad I was arrested; otherwise, I would have committed suicide’ Subrat was arrested on 24 September. He said, “I have no regret about arranging my father's murder; he was debauched. I only regret that he should not have been stabbed to death like this. I did not want to have him murdered in this way. I felt guilty when Shalu went to jail, and I had started taking sleeping pills. If the police had not caught me, I would have committed suicide.” Subrat went on to say, "My father had affairs with several women. I was afraid he might marry one of them and bring her home. She would become a stakeholder in the property. I was dependent on others for every rupee, while my father showed me pictures of himself partying with girls in Goa. I was in debt of around ₹40 lakh. My father gave me only ₹40,000 as pocket money. He treated me like a servant."

stories.title: UP youth tells DM, ‘Ask Indra Dev to stop rain’:Says rain causing problems; ‘I don’t have God’s number, you make divine contact’
stories.summary: Troubled by the rain in Hardoi, a young man has filed an unusual complaint. He complained to the district magistrate (DM) against Indradev, the rain god. The young man said that Indradev had been causing continuous rain for several hours without any prior warning. The rain was sometimes heavy and sometimes light. This had disrupted normal life. Waterlogging on roads, in lanes and in low-lying areas was making it difficult for people to travel. In the complaint, the young man said, 'I do not know Indradev's phone number. The DM should contact him through official channels and instruct him to stop the rain so that the people of the district can get relief.' The complaint was filed on the IGRS, or Integrated Grievance Redressal System, public grievance portal on 26 September. The complainant is named Suraj Tiwari. He is a social worker by profession. Suraj is a resident of Nevadas Paras village in the Mallawan block. Now read the complete complaint verbatim... Suraj Tiwari said in his complaint: Indradev has been causing continuous rain without any prior notice, putting the general public to unnecessary inconvenience. As a result, it has become difficult for people to leave their homes and their daily activities are also being affected. Therefore, it is requested that the matter be taken seriously and that the concerned Indradev be issued the necessary directions to immediately control the rain, so that the residents of the district can get relief. The complainant does not know Indradev's mobile number, so kindly send the notice/directions through his available divine means of contact. 250 mm of Rain in Hardoi in three days In Hardoi, rain continued for three consecutive days from the night of 24 September to 27 September. More than 250 mm of rain was recorded in just four days. More than 20 houses collapsed during the rain. Twelve people have died after walls and trees fell. Impact of the rain will decrease significantly over the next 24 hours Varanasi meteorologist Manoj Srivastava said that the cyclone which originated in the Bay of Bengal had weakened after passing through Uttar Pradesh. The rain that continued for four days has now begun to subside. The impact of the rain will reduce significantly over the next 24 hours. Only the Terai areas bordering Nepal will receive light rain. The weather will remain clear across the state at the beginning of October. There will be bright sunshine.

stories.title: MCA graduate steals 30kg silver in Kanpur:Panicked during police questioning; asked court, ‘Am I wanted?’
stories.summary: Police have arrested MCA graduate Sudhanshu Agrawal in connection with the theft of 30 kg of silver from a bullion trader’s home in Kanpur. According to police, Agrawal, whose house is just 500 metres from the trader’s home, allegedly committed the theft to repay a gambling and betting debt of ₹10 lakh. DCP East Satyajeet Gupta said the accused was arrested from Phalmandi at around 12 noon on Sunday and had buried the stolen silver at different spots in the soil at Nana Rao Park, about half a kilometre from his home. Based on information provided by him, police recovered around 22 kg of silver. Here is the full story Teenager Kishore Singh, a resident of Chatai Mohal in the Filkhana area, owns a shop named Priyanka Jewellers in Chowk Sarafa. The shop is located opposite Kalyan Bhawan. Kishore Singh said that at around 8:30 p.m. on 12 September, he returned home from the shop carrying 30 kg of silver worth ₹75 lakh and ₹75,000 in cash. At around 9:30 p.m. on 18 September, his son Abhay went to park his motorcycle inside the house. During this, he moved a wooden plank kept near the cupboard. He then noticed that the cupboard was open. The silver and cash kept inside were missing. The police were then informed by calling 112. ACP Kotwali Amit Kumar Pandey and Filkhana police reached the spot. The police began an investigation. Sudhanshu was seen roaming around the house on 15 September The DCP said four CCTV cameras were installed in the lane where bullion trader Kishore Singh's house is located. Police examined footage from CCTV cameras installed in the surrounding area. The footage showed a young man carrying a bag and roaming around the jeweller's house on 15 September. After some time, he was seen leaving the area with the bag slung over his shoulder. However, his face was not clearly visible in the initial footage. Police then began making enquiries at his house and in the surrounding area. He went to court himself and asked, ‘Am I wanted?’ After questioning local people, police suspected Sudhanshu Agrawal. His house was also barely 500 metres from the businessman's residence. Police questioned Sudhanshu, which frightened him. Five days ago, he filed an application in court himself, asking whether he was wanted in any case. The court sent the application to police for investigation, which further increased his suspicion. Police then arrested him from the fruit market on Sunday. Seven kilograms less silver recovered; cash not found Police have recovered 22.348 kg of stolen silver from Sudhanshu Agarwal. The trader had complained that 30 kg of silver and ₹75,000 in cash had been stolen. Police are investigating where the remaining silver went and what happened to the cash. According to police, after completing an MCA, Sudhanshu began working at a company in Kalyanpur. He used to bet online. His debts gradually grew. He then planned the theft. Police are now investigating which app or website he used for betting and who had lent him the money. The doors were open and the key was kept in the cupboard Bullion trader Kishore Singh said they usually do not keep the shop's jewellery and cash at home. However, by coincidence, the silver and cash had been kept at home that day. Their house has three floors. The family lives on the upper floors, while the ground floor remains vacant. The silver and cash were kept in a cupboard in a room on the ground floor. The cupboard key was also kept there. The main gates of the house and the room were open. The thief took advantage of this.

stories.title: ‘They replaced knee she walked on’:Elderly woman’s son in Lucknow alleges signatures taken on blank paper as formality
stories.summary: A family has claimed that a doctor operated on the wrong leg of an elderly woman at a private hospital in Lucknow on Monday. Rajeshwari, a resident of Rajajipuram, was admitted for surgery on her left knee, which had been causing her problems for several days, but her son Manoj Kumar alleges that the doctor operated on her right knee instead. According to the family, she was admitted to a private nursing home on September 8 and shifted to Health City Hospital (Remedy Medicity) the next day under the Ayushman scheme. The family further alleged that ₹65,000 was charged separately for the implant and that they were threatened when they questioned the doctor about the alleged mistake. Manoj said that he went to the ICU to meet his mother the day after the operation. During the meeting, Rajeshwari allegedly told him that the doctor had operated on her other leg. The family then questioned the doctor about the surgery, following which they allegedly faced threats. The family has raised questions over how the wrong leg was operated on and why the surgery was performed on the leg that was not reportedly causing the problem. They have sought an explanation regarding the alleged medical error and the circumstances surrounding the surgery. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to the victim's son and gathered details of the entire incident. Read the report... 'They operated on the other leg instead of the one that was hurting' Manoj says that, before the surgery, his nephew was made to sign some plain sheets of paper and forms in the name of completing paperwork. The hospital is now saying that it had already been explained that the surgery would be performed on this leg. Manoj alleges that Dr C.P. Gupta is responsible for such serious negligence involving his elderly mother. Following the negligence, his mother has become completely bedridden. She is now unable to do any of her own work. Manoj filed a complaint against the doctor at the Gomtinagar police station. He also submitted a complaint to the CMO's office, but says that no action has been taken in the matter so far. ₹2.5 lakh deducted from Ayushman card; neither police nor CMO listening Earlier, the elderly woman's grandson Ayush had said that his grandmother, Rajeshwari (70), was admitted to Aadya Hospital on 8 September for surgery on her left knee. Saying that the surgery would involve higher expenses, they shifted her to Health City Hospital on 11 September for the operation under the Ayushman card scheme. Dr C.P. Gupta performed the surgery that evening. The operation was supposed to be performed on the left knee, but the right knee was operated on instead. She was discharged on 14 September. During this period, ₹65,000 was deposited in cash and a payment of ₹2.50 lakh was made through the Ayushman card. After being discharged, she submitted an application in Gomti Nagar on the same day requesting that an FIR be registered, but the FIR was not registered. She then submitted an application to the CMO on 16 September, but no action was taken. She has now lodged a complaint with Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak. Read what was written in the complaint: In his complaint to the police, the elderly woman’s son, Manoj Kumar, alleged that his mother was hurriedly taken to the operation theatre, where preparations were made to perform surgery on her right knee. She reportedly questioned the medical staff, saying that the problem was in her left knee and asking whether it would be treated. According to the complaint, the doctors present in the operation theatre allegedly told her to remain silent. When she asked them to call her family members, they allegedly refused. The doctors then administered anaesthesia and proceeded with the surgery. Manoj claimed that after the operation, the family learned that the doctor had operated on the right knee instead of the left knee. Videos recorded by the family members have emerged The family members of the elderly woman who was affected had recorded several videos of the entire incident. Those videos have now emerged. In one video, the family members can be seen alleging that the doctor verbally abused them when they went to complain. In another video, the doctor can be heard saying, "You people are harassing the doctor; this is a non-bailable offence." In another video, the family members are seen calling the police. They can be heard saying that the doctor performed the wrong operation here and is now hurling abuses. Another video shows the elderly woman who was affected. She is sitting on a bed, with several people present there. When asked, the elderly woman pointed to the knee that is causing her pain. Her leg appears to be moving in the middle. Hospital leased to another group Health City MD Dr Sandeep Kapoor said in a video statement, "We have leased our Vijay Khand hospital to the Remedy Medicity Group." Care is essential when treating the elderly Dr Ashish Kumar, in-charge of the KGMU Limb Centre and head of the Department of Orthopaedics, said, "There is a belief that surgery is performed first on the leg or knee in which the patient has greater difficulty. Apart from this" The recovered amount must be returned within seven days Lucknow CMO Dr NB Singh said an expert doctors' panel had been formed to investigate the matter. The investigation found evidence that the elderly woman's relatives had signed a consent form at the doctor's clinic. The form mentions only the operation on the right leg. There is no clinical problem with the knee in that leg after the surgery either. Attempts were made several times to contact Dr CP Gupta, who performed the surgery in this case, and obtain his version, but he could not be reached.
