stories.title: Ajay Rai climbs barricades in Lucknow:Congress workers clash with police in rain during protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
stories.summary: Congress workers protesting in Lucknow, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, clashed with police on Thursday. The confrontation led to pushing and shoving as the protesters attempted to march towards the Uttar Pradesh Assembly and the Chief Minister’s residence. The police stopped the protesters with barricades about 200 metres into their march. Angry over being stopped, Uttar Pradesh Congress president Ajay Rai, MLA Aradhana Mishra and other party workers climbed the barricades and raised slogans. A scuffle then broke out between the police and Congress workers. Congress leader Shiv Pandey suffered an injury to his leg. He alleged that he was injured by a police baton. The situation remained tense at the spot, with Congress workers continuing their protest in the rain. Women protesters were also seen carrying posters with the slogan, “Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod”. CEC’s Meerut, Varanasi visits postponed The Election Commission has postponed two programmes in Uttar Pradesh that CEC Gyanesh Kumar was scheduled to attend. The first programme was scheduled in Meerut on September 25, while the second was planned in Varanasi on September 28. The EC said both programmes had been postponed on September 21 and that the decision was not related to the ongoing controversy. See four pictures of the protest... What is the controversy over removal of the CEC? According to a September 23 report by The Indian Express, two Election Commissioners had raised written objections over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) at least 14 times in the past 10 months. Four of these objections were raised on the same day. The Election Commission, however, said such objections were part of the normal procedure and that all final decisions, including those related to the SIR, were taken unanimously.

stories.title: Women wrestlers move Delhi HC over Brij Bhushan Singh's acquittal:Petitioners call trial court's order in sexual harassment case 'regressive'
stories.summary: Four women wrestlers have approached the Rouse Avenue Court against the acquittal of former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) president and BJP leader Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh in the sexual harassment case. They have challenged the 3 August, 2026, order of the trial court that cleared Singh and former WFI assistant secretary Vinod Tomar of all charges. According to news agency ANI, the wrestlers have filed an appeal before the Rouse Avenue Court. They have described the trial court's decision as "archaic" and argued that it was based on old and stereotypical ideas about how victims of sexual harassment are expected to behave. The appeal is likely to be heard on September 26. The wrestlers have said that the trial court did not properly assess the evidence and instead relied on assumptions about their conduct after the alleged incidents. Wrestlers challenge Trial Court's reasoning In their appeal, the women wrestlers have argued that the August 3 judgment is not legally sustainable. They said the evidence available on record was assessed incorrectly and selectively. They also claimed that the judgment was based on "conjectures and surmises" and did not properly apply established legal principles. The wrestlers said the evidence should have been examined fairly while keeping their circumstances in mind. The appeal further argues that the court relied on "archaic and stereotypical assumptions" about the "expected" behaviour of victims of sexual assault and harassment. Court had questioned delay and conduct While acquitting Singh, the trial court had considered the wrestlers' long silence, their continued cordial relations with Singh and differences in their statements as factors that raised doubts about the prosecution's case. The court also referred to photographs showing that some of the complainants had invited Singh to family functions and weddings. It had noted that the wrestlers may have feared damage to their careers because Singh was then the WFI president, but questioned why they continued to maintain cordial relations with him for years. The women wrestlers have challenged this reasoning in their appeal, arguing that a victim's behaviour after an alleged incident should not be judged on fixed assumptions. Brij Bhushan and Vinod Tomar were acquitted Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate (ACJM) Ashwini Panwar acquitted Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh on August 3, 2026. The court also acquitted Vinod Tomar. The proceedings were held in camera. The court had said that the prosecution failed to prove the charges beyond reasonable doubt. Singh was acquitted under IPC Sections 354, 354A and 506 (Part-I), while Tomar was acquitted under Section 506 (Part-I). Delhi Police had filed chargesheet Delhi Police had filed a chargesheet against Singh under IPC Sections 354, 354A, 354D and 506(1). Section 109 was also invoked against Tomar. The allegations were made by women wrestlers and related to alleged incidents between 2016 and 2019 at the WFI office, Singh's official residence and locations abroad. The police had also filed a closure/cancellation report in a separate POCSO case involving a minor wrestler. The latest appeal now puts the 3 August acquittal back before the Rouse Avenue Court, with the matter expected to be taken up on 26 September.

stories.title: Budaun youth dies after neck gets severed on tin sheet:Blood gushed out, brother tied neck with gamcha; became father 8 days ago
stories.summary: A 24-year-old man died after his neck was severed by a tin sheet while he was travelling on a motorcycle in Budaun. The incident occurred near Jafarpur village in the Islamnagar police station area at around 9 pm on Thursday (24 Sept). The deceased, Ankush Singh, was travelling to a factory with his brother Rakesh and neighbour Dilip when a tin sheet being unloaded from a pickup vehicle fell onto their motorcycle. Brother tries to stop bleeding, takes him to hospital According to the information available, workers were unloading tin sheets from a pickup when one of the sheets slipped from their hands and spun towards the road. It fell on the three motorcycle riders as they passed by. Ankush suffered a severe neck injury. His brother Rakesh reportedly held his injured neck and tied it with a gamcha in an attempt to stop the bleeding before taking him to a hospital. However, Ankush died before reaching the hospital. Know the full details of the incident Ankush Singh (24), a resident of Jafarpur village in the Islamnagar police station area, was the third of five siblings. His father is Prem Singh. Ankush was on his way to a factory in Chandausi, Sambhal district, for his night shift. His cousin Rakesh, son of Chandrabhan, and neighbour Dilip, son of Ram Bharose, were travelling with him on the motorcycle. Tin sheet slips from workers’ hands, hits passing motorcycle The incident took place around 9 pm on Thursday (24 Sept) near Jafarpur village, in front of the house of a former village head. Some workers were unloading tin sheets from a pickup vehicle when one of the sheets suddenly slipped from their hands. The sheet fell onto the road and spun towards the opposite side, hitting the motorcycle carrying Ankush, Rakesh and Dilip as they passed by. Ankush was riding the motorcycle when the sharp edge of the tin sheet struck his neck, causing a severe injury. Rakesh and Dilip, who were riding pillion, also sustained injuries. The two immediately helped Ankush and rushed him to a private hospital in Chandausi. Doctors examined him and declared him dead. Rakesh and Dilip are undergoing treatment. Ankush became a father just eight days before his death Ankush’s death left his family devastated. He had married Priyanka around a year and a half ago, and she gave birth to their son just eight days before the accident. The family was preparing for the baby’s naming ceremony and was celebrating his arrival. However, Ankush’s sudden death turned the celebrations into mourning. The naming ceremony could not be held. Police begin investigation, search for pickup driver and workers Islamnagar Inspector Dhananjay Singh said, “The post-mortem examination of Ankush’s body is being conducted. A case will be registered based on the complaint filed by his family.” He added, “Police are also searching for the pickup driver and the workers who were unloading the tin sheets.”

stories.title: Shah says Yogi crushed SP’s lawlessness:‘All mafias wiped out’; toured in same vehicle, spoke at length on stage
stories.summary: Home Minister Amit Shah inaugurated the UP International Trade Show on Friday. He said, “There was a time when mafias ruled Uttar Pradesh. The Yogi government has wiped out the hooliganism of the SP-BSP. Now, BrahMos missiles made in UP are keeping Pakistan awake.” He said: Rifles made in Amethi have already kept Naxalites and terrorists awake. During the SP-BSP rule, there was an industry of crime. A cottage industry of country-made pistols and guns had flourished. Today, the defence corridor has been built in place of the country-made arms industry. Shah reached the expo with CM Yogi in a golf cart at around 11:30 am. The two leaders visited stalls and took information about the products. Both leaders also spoke for a long time on the stage. See the pictures… The trade show, which will continue till September 29, is being held for the fourth time. Japan, Russia, Vietnam, Austria, Singapore and Belarus are participating as partner countries this year. More than 600 buyers from 85 countries are expected to attend. The organisers expect business worth ₹2 lakh crore this time. Along with traditional UP products, companies from the electronics, EV, defence, IT and food processing sectors will participate. More than 2,500 stalls have been set up this year. Under the ‘One District, One Cuisine’ initiative, traditional dishes and local food culture from different districts of the state will also be showcased. Seminars and cultural programmes will be held every day. More than 4.5 lakh people are expected to visit the trade show over five days.

stories.title: Father refuses to accept daughter after High Court acquittal:Woman was sentenced to death for drowning three children in Auraiya; court overturns conviction
stories.summary: “My daughter killed the children. We will neither have any relationship with her nor keep her in our home. We do not want to accept her. I never met her after the children died and did not fight her case either.” These are the words of Pramod, father of Priyanka from Auraiya, who was acquitted by the Allahabad High Court after being sentenced to death for allegedly drowning three of her children. The sessions court had sentenced Priyanka to death. However, on Wednesday (September 23), the High Court overturned the conviction and acquitted both Priyanka and her co-accused, Ashish alias Danny. The High Court also rejected the testimony of Priyanka’s surviving eight-year-old son, citing contradictions and other shortcomings in the prosecution's case. The Dainik Bhaskar team visited Priyanka’s home, around 12 km from the district headquarters, and spoke to her family. Priyanka began living with her cousin brother-in-law after husband’s death Priyanka, a resident of Baraua village, married Avneesh of Luia village in Etawah in 2009. The couple had four sons — Sonu, Aditya, Madhav and Mangal. Avneesh died of electrocution in 2020. After his death, Priyanka began living with her cousin brother-in-law, Ashish alias Danny. Villagers allegedly taunted the two for living together, after which they moved to a rented house in Banarsidas locality in the city with the children. Ashish started working at a salon. According to the family, disputes later began over the upbringing of the children. Ashish allegedly assaulted Priyanka and the children and repeatedly told her that he would stay with her only if she killed the children. Woman sentenced to death, brother-in-law to life imprisonment According to the prosecution case, on June 27, 2024, Priyanka allegedly threw her four children into the Sengur river after being distressed by Ashish’s taunts. Three children drowned, while eight-year-old Sonu was rescued by villagers. Sonu later testified against his mother in court. On July 10, 2025, the Sessions Court sentenced Priyanka to death and Ashish to life imprisonment. Both were also fined ₹1 lakh each. Trial court had called incident ‘rarest of rare’ While awarding the death sentence, ADJ Saif Ahmed had described the incident as a “rarest of rare” case. The court had observed that a woman who could kill her own sons had no right to live in society and questioned how anyone could be certain that a child would be safe with his mother after such an incident. High Court cites contradictions and investigation lapses While overturning the trial court’s decision, the High Court pointed to several shortcomings in the prosecution’s case. The court observed that: The High Court concluded that the prosecution had failed to prove the charges against Priyanka and Ashish. It therefore set aside the lower court’s judgment and acquitted both accused. Aunt raised Priyanka after her mother’s death Priyanka’s father Pramod, uncle Kanhaiyalal and aunt Geeta Devi live in Baraua village, her parental home. Geeta Devi said she had raised Priyanka after her mother died when she was around one-and-a-half years old. Priyanka also had a brother, Pawan, who later died of an illness. Geeta said she had visited Priyanka once and found that she regretted what had happened. Father says he will have no relationship with daughter Pramod initially refused to speak to the Dainik Bhaskar team. He later said that although Priyanka had been acquitted, he still believed she had killed the children. “I have neither gone to meet her nor fought her case. I have no relationship with her. There is no place for her in my home. I will never accept her,” he said. Both families did not pursue the case The families of both Priyanka and Ashish did not provide legal representation, following which government lawyers were appointed for them. According to the report, no family member visited either accused in jail. Priyanka remained calm in custody, while Ashish appeared uncomfortable and had told the court that he had been framed. Surviving son’s testimony that led to conviction During the trial, Sonu told the judge that he had earlier been living with his paternal aunt in Etawah for his studies. After his father died of electrocution, his mother took all the children to their maternal grandparents’ home. He said Ashish, whom the children called Danny uncle, used to visit them and would spend hours talking to his mother. He alleged that his mother sometimes did not give him food and also beat him. He said his younger siblings were also often left without food and would cry. According to Sonu’s testimony, his mother later said they would go to Danny’s house. After they moved there, disputes began between Priyanka and Ashish. Sonu said Ashish repeatedly asked her to leave the children at their maternal grandmother’s house. Mother took children to river after preparing them for school Sonu told the court that Priyanka and Ashish had a major argument on the night of June 26, 2024. The next morning, he said, his mother got all the children ready and took them in an autorickshaw, telling them they were going to their grandmother’s house. When they reached the river, she got out with the children and took them towards the water. Sonu alleged that she then began pushing his brothers’ faces into the water. He said Aditya, Madhav and Mangal died, while he was also held underwater. Sonu says he held his breath and escaped Sonu told the court that he suddenly remembered Khatu Shyam Baba and held his breath. Believing that all the children had died, his mother started leaving. He said that when she moved ahead, he escaped and ran away. When Priyanka turned around and saw him, she allegedly chased him. Sonu said he ran directly to the village head’s house, after which his mother left. The village head informed the police and the children’s uncle. The bodies of the three boys were later recovered from the river. SP says action will follow if investigation lapses are confirmed The High Court’s order has highlighted alleged negligence by investigating officer Bhupendra Singh Rathi, including several facts that were not covered during the investigation. The village head was the first person to inform the police about the incident but was not examined as a witness. Auraiya SP Abhishek Bharti said the police had not yet received a copy of the High Court order. He said action would be taken if any negligence was found after examining the order.

stories.title: 20 hours of rain in Lucknow:Half of UP hit by showers, petrol tanker swept away in flooded river in Lalitpur; schools shut in 4 districts
stories.summary: Weather has deteriorated in Uttar Pradesh due to Cyclone ‘Arnab’ formed over the Bay of Bengal. More than half of the state is receiving rain, ranging from heavy to light, while skies remain overcast. It is dark-like during the day in several areas. Strong winds have flattened crops at several places, while water has accumulated in fields. Weather conditions have worsened in 40 cities, including Lucknow, Kanpur, Unnao, Varanasi, Prayagraj and Jaunpur. Lucknow has been receiving rain accompanied by strong winds for the past 20 hours. There is also a slight chill in the air. Due to the bad weather, schools up to Class 12 have been closed in Ayodhya and Sultanpur, while schools up to Class 8 have been closed in Jaunpur and Gonda. In Lalitpur, the Jamni River is in spate due to continuous rain. A bridge near Kujhan Ghat was submerged. A petrol tanker got stuck amid the strong current in the morning and was swept away before getting trapped between the bridge and the river. Police reached the spot after being informed, and the tanker was pulled out with the help of villagers. A thunderstorm and rain alert has been issued for 65 districts today. See pictures of the rain… Ayodhya has been receiving intermittent heavy rain for the past 36 hours, accompanied by strong winds. Crops have fallen in rural areas due to the weather. Sitapur has been receiving heavy rain since late Thursday night. Continuous rain has brought down temperatures. Varanasi has been receiving drizzle since morning, along with strong winds. The pleasant weather has drawn crowds to the ghats. In Lalitpur, a tanker was swept away by the strong river current. It lost control while crossing the bridge, slipped and ended up hanging over the river. According to meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh, a low-pressure area has formed over the Bay of Bengal and has crossed the Andhra Pradesh and Odisha coasts. At the same time, activity in the westerly winds has intensified. Due to the system, rain accompanied by thunderstorms is expected across Uttar Pradesh until September 27–28. Daytime temperatures may drop by 5–8°C, bringing increased chill to the weather. See where rain is expected today…

stories.title: ‘Dreaming is important, but Akhilesh has no Raj Yog’:BJP MP Ravi Kishan in Gorakhpur; says Rath Yatra will show UP’s development
stories.summary: Gorakhpur BJP MP Ravi Kishan took a jibe at Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav over his remarks during the PDA Rath Yatra that the BJP would be defeated by the “bulldozer of votes”. Akhilesh made the remarks during the launch of the PDA Rath Yatra in Rae Bareli on September 24. Ravi Kishan said dreaming was important, but claimed that Akhilesh Yadav’s horoscope showed no “rajyog” for the next several years. He also said people would decide Akhilesh’s political future and claimed that he should forget about the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election. ‘I dream too, but Akhilesh has no rajyog’: Ravi Kishan Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, Ravi Kishan said, “I dream too. He (Akhilesh) dreams too. But all the astrologers and priests who have studied Akhilesh’s horoscope have found no rajyog in it. There will be none for many years.” He added that the people would write Akhilesh’s political “horoscope” themselves and said the SP chief should forget about the 2027 election. Ravi Kishan says people will decide SP’s political future Ravi Kishan said Akhilesh Yadav had failed to deliver when he had the opportunity to govern. He claimed that people were now assessing the work of political parties and would decide their future. He alleged that the Samajwadi Party would face a major defeat and said people did not want to return to what he described as the “rule of mafias and goons” during the SP’s tenure. Praises Akhilesh’s Rath Yatra Ravi Kishan also stated that SP workers should continue with their Rath Yatra and travel across Uttar Pradesh to see the development carried out under the Narendra Modi and Yogi Adityanath governments. He claimed that they would see development work and improvements in law and order across the state. Invites Akhilesh to visit major development projects Ravi Kishan also said Akhilesh Yadav should visit Ayodhya and see the Ram temple, as well as the Maa Vindhyachal Corridor and Baba Vishwanath Corridor. He further urged Akhilesh to visit renovated schools and Kalyan Mandapams built in Gorakhpur, saying he could see the development work carried out there.

stories.title: 558kg opium worth ₹10.80 crore destroyed in Varanasi:Jaitpura Police seized it in 2012; disposed of at Ghazipur central factory
stories.summary: Jaitpura police in Varanasi destroyed 558 kg of opium valued at ₹10.80 crore. The narcotic was seized by the police in 2012 during the investigation of a case. To dispose of the seized opium as per regulations, a police team took it to the Central Opium and Alkaloid Factory in Ghazipur. Action taken under Operation Dahan ACP Chetnaganj Shubham Singh said, “The action was carried out under Uttar Pradesh Police’s Operation Dahan, aimed at disposing of narcotics seized in cases and stored for long periods.” He added, “A team led by Jaitpura Station House Officer Upendra Pratap Singh transported the seized opium to Ghazipur for disposal as part of the process.” Seized opium weighs 558 kg, valued at ₹10.80 crore After reaching the factory, all the seized opium packets were weighed as per procedure. The total weight was found to be 558 kg, with an estimated value of around ₹10.80 crore, according to police. Opium seized in 2012 kept in safe custody The ACP said that the opium had been seized by local police in 2012 during the investigation of a case and was subsequently kept in safe custody. The seized narcotic was taken to the Central Opium and Alkaloid Factory under the supervision of the Drug Disposal Committee. It was disposed of after completing all prescribed procedures. After completing the disposal process, the police team returned to Varanasi from Ghazipur. According to police, the opium seized in 2012 had been kept in safe custody as part of the legal proceedings in the case. It has now been destroyed after completing the prescribed procedures. Disposal of seized narcotics to continue under Operation Dahan Police officials stated that the disposal of narcotics seized in various cases will continue in accordance with the prescribed rules under Operation Dahan.

stories.title: Bank manager shoots himself in moving car, dies:Fired gun near heart in Jaunpur; bullet pierced back and lodged in seat
stories.summary: The manager of Union Bank in Jaunpur took his own life late on Thursday night. He pressed a country-made pistol against his heart while driving and shot himself. The bullet pierced his back and lodged in the seat. After he was shot, the Tata Sierra went out of control and crashed into a divider. Passers-by and nearby residents reached the spot. They broke the car window and pulled the manager out. He was taken to hospital, where he died. Police found a suicide note in the car. The incident took place near Prabhu Dhaba in the Baksha police station area, 15 km from the district headquarters. Durgesh Srivastava, 40, was a resident of Gudamba in Lucknow. He lived with his wife, Rachna, in the Van Vihar area of Jaunpur city. He was posted at the Sarai Padri branch in the Sujanganj police station area, 30 km from the city. His wife Rachna said, "He had been under stress for a week. We asked him the reason, but he did not tell us anything." 'We thought there had been an accident' People working at the dhaba said, "We were working when a car crashed into the highway divider. We thought there had been an accident. We ran to the spot and, after breaking the window, found a man sitting inside the car, covered in blood. He had been shot. A country-made pistol was lying beside the body. We then called the police." ASP Atish Kumar Singh said- Police arrived after receiving information about the incident. The manager was taken to the district hospital, where he died during treatment. The forensic team examined the car and collected evidence. One body has been sent for post-mortem.

stories.title: Akhilesh says ‘this election is Lodhi vs Yogi’:‘Vote bulldozer will finish BJP’; calls them fake Hindus
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav launched his PDA Rath for the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections on Thursday. Targeting the BJP in Raebareli, he said, “This is a PDA storm. A PDA wave is sweeping through the state. In Raebareli, it seems this election is not just PDA versus BJP; it could also be ‘Lodhi versus Yogi’.” “This time, the people’s vote bulldozer will run over them. This vote bulldozer will bring them down forever. It will not just defeat them, but will work to wipe out forever those who practise such negative politics. “The dominant people who consider themselves powerful and the supremacists we are fighting are not a new challenge. This struggle is thousands of years old. We stand with the weak and deprived. We stand to protect reservation. We stand to protect Indianness. These people do not believe in the Constitution or the law. BJP leaders are fake Hindus.” Before this, Akhilesh reached Nigohan in Lucknow by car. From there, he travelled by rath for 50 km to address a public meeting at the GIC ground in Raebareli. For the first time at one of his rallies, two cranes were brought in to welcome Akhilesh. A 21-kg garland was presented to him using the cranes. Key points from Akhilesh’s speech On the PDA Rath: The rath has been a symbol of Kurukshetra in Indian culture. Lord Krishna also imparted the knowledge of the Gita through a rath. Through this rath, I declare that those who are oppressed are the PDA. On the 2024 Lok Sabha elections: Those who harass and persecute people will not be spared in this election. We defeated them in 2024 and will defeat them again in 2027. This time, they will be pushed even further away, and efforts will be made to remove discrimination from society. On alleged theft of Ram temple offerings: Crores of devotees make offerings at Ayodhya with faith. Cases of theft have come to light there. Those stealing have also been caught on CCTV. On the Election Commission: “The entire truth about them has come out, and they are working like puppets. Perhaps nothing this shameful has ever happened in a democracy, as what this Election Commission has done. There should be an investigation into whose instructions the Election Commission was acting on. The people of the country have the right to know.” On corruption in the expressway: They (BJP leaders) say corruption existed earlier. I want to say that whenever Mother Ganga calls you, do not travel on the Ganga Expressway. If you drive fast, you will end up bouncing along the road. A 63-km expressway in Kanpur was built at a cost of ₹4,700 crore. Potholes appeared, and the road started breaking soon after its inauguration. Those who built it turned out to be associated with the BJP. The company was blacklisted. If you drive fast on it, you will hurt your back and develop stomach pain. On the poster war in Raebareli: Posters were put up by those who change colours as soon as I left my house today. The first people on this earth to change colours are those in the administration. They have nothing to do with law and rules. I assure you that those who have not followed the law will be punished as soon as our government is formed. Allegation of discrimination: On one side are the oppressed, and on the other are those who harass them. They divide society and discriminate. They get homes and temples washed with Ganga water. When PDA members go there, they face discrimination. PDA members are standing to protect the Constitution, law, and democracy. Reached MLA Rahul Lodhi’s residence After the public meeting, Akhilesh went to the residence of SP MLA Rahul Lodhi. Here, he met Samajwadi Chhatrasabha workers who had clashed with ABVP workers and police on September 17. On the way, he offered prayers at a Hanuman temple and waved a mace. Around 2,000–3,000 workers accompanied his rath, along with around 200 vehicles. Workers danced to DJ music and raised slogans as they followed the rath. The rath yatra caused a traffic jam on the Lucknow-Raebareli Highway, in which the convoy of Yogi government minister Dinesh Singh got stuck. Meanwhile, posters targeting Akhilesh were put up in Raebareli ahead of the rath yatra. The posters carried pictures of Akhilesh alongside Azam Khan, Atiq Ahmed and Mukhtar Ansari. They read: ‘Akhilesh Yadav, go back’ and ‘Akhilesh’s mafias, mafia’s Akhilesh’. See 3 pictures: Why did Akhilesh start the PDA Rath Yatra from Raebareli? Know the significance… The SP president began his campaign for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections with the PDA Rath Yatra from Raebareli, a traditional Congress stronghold. There are four reasons behind the choice: Advantage in seat-sharing talks: Raebareli is Rahul Gandhi’s parliamentary constituency. By starting the campaign here, Akhilesh Yadav is signalling the Samajwadi Party’s grassroots strength to its alliance partner Congress, potentially strengthening its position in the upcoming seat-sharing discussions. Support for workers: After alleged mistreatment of Samajwadi Chhatrasabha leaders in Raebareli, Akhilesh chose the area to boost workers’ morale and send a message that he stands with them. Strengthening the PDA equation: Through the yatra, he is seeking to mobilise the ‘Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak’ (PDA) and ‘peedit’ sections of society. Strong Assembly record: The Raebareli Lok Sabha constituency has five Assembly seats, of which the SP had won four. After Manoj Pandey joined the BJP, the number fell to three. His main aim is to reactivate this strong base ahead of the elections. Ajay Rai says anyone can campaign anywhere On Akhilesh’s rath yatra, UP Congress president Ajay Rai said anyone can go anywhere to campaign. “We are certainly doing our work and are now standing firmly with the people in their joys and sorrows. People are joining the Congress in large numbers. Today, the entire country is looking towards Rahul Gandhi. Rahul Gandhi is strongly raising issues concerning the country and fighting for the country as well,” he said. Mercedes bus modified into PDA Rath at a cost of ₹1.5 crore A nine-year-old Mercedes bus has been modified into the PDA Rath at a cost of ₹1.5 crore. The rath has a meeting hall and pantry with seating for 8–10 people. It also has a hydraulic lift that allows Akhilesh to stand on the roof and address people. ‘Samajwadi PDA Yatra’ is written on the PDA Rath. Its slogans include: ‘The banner of social justice will fly, PDA will bring change.’ The bus carries pictures of several social reformers, including Dr BR Ambedkar.

stories.title: Why sleeper buses turn into fireballs:Banned in Western countries; accidents continue in India, yet no ban
stories.summary: At 9.30pm on September 23, a luxury sleeper bus left Delhi’s Kashmiri Gate for Mahoba in Uttar Pradesh. At around 11.30pm, it caught fire on the Yamuna Expressway. Nine passengers were burnt to death. The bodies were so badly burnt that they could not be identified. Looking at similar accidents in the past shows that these buses can turn into fireballs after something as minor as a short circuit or a collision with another vehicle. Sleeper buses are banned in several countries, including England, Germany and China, but not in India. The question is: Why are sleeper buses still not banned in India despite repeated accidents? How can these buses turn into fireballs after even a minor accident? Read the answers to these questions in today’s UP Explainer… Question 1: Why do sleeper buses turn into fireballs after a small short circuit? Why are there so many deaths? Answer: There are three major reasons... 1. The interior allows fire to spread rapidly Sleeper buses require wiring throughout the vehicle to install the air-conditioning unit. In the event of a short circuit or accident, the AC motor and wiring can easily catch fire. The gases used for cooling in AC systems (R-32 or R-410A) are highly flammable. If the gas pipe develops a leak, it can cause the fire to flare up. 2. Night travel and tired drivers make it harder to handle emergencies Most sleeper buses operate on long routes and travel at night. This increases the possibility of drivers becoming tired or falling asleep. In several accidents, drivers have reportedly been suspected of dozing off. For example, 26 people were killed in a bus accident in Buldhana, Maharashtra, on July 1, 2023. SP Sunil Kadasne suspected that the driver may have felt dizzy or fallen asleep. Road safety expert Bharat Dogra says passengers also have slower response times at night. In an accident, the first two minutes can sometimes make the difference between life and death. A passenger sitting up, even if drowsy, is likely to respond better than someone who is lying down and asleep. 3. Improper modification of sleeper buses During bus modifications, Automotive Industry Standard (AIS) requirements are often not followed. Emergency exits may be removed or blocked during modifications. After the Jaisalmer bus accident on October 14, 2025, the Dainik Bhaskar team carried out a reality check of sleeper buses in Rajasthan. More than 50 buses were inspected. Emergency exits were found blocked, and none of the buses had fire-safety equipment. Question 2: Is there a particular pattern in sleeper bus accidents? Answer: Yes. More than 100 people have died in 10 major sleeper bus accidents over the past five years. Nine of these accidents occurred at night, with most taking place between midnight and 6am. In most cases, the death toll increased because passengers could not get out in time. May 22, 2026: A sleeper bus travelling from Gurugram, Haryana, to Kanpur collided with a truck in Firozabad and caught fire. The driver and conductor were burnt alive, while around 25 people suffered burn injuries. March 13, 2026: A sleeper AC bus travelling from Jaisalmer, Rajasthan, to Ahmedabad, Gujarat, caught fire, killing one person and injuring nine. October 24, 2025: A bus travelling from Hyderabad to Bengaluru collided with a motorcycle near Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh, and caught fire. Twenty passengers were burnt to death. October 14, 2025: A moving sleeper bus travelling from Jaisalmer to Jodhpur in Rajasthan suddenly caught fire. Twenty people were burnt alive. May 15, 2025: A bus travelling from Begusarai in Bihar to Delhi caught fire on Kisan Path in Lucknow. Five people, including two children, were killed. October 19, 2024: Twelve people were killed when a sleeper bus collided with a tempo in Dholpur, Rajasthan. The accident occurred at around 11pm. November 8, 2023: A sleeper bus travelling from Jaipur to Delhi caught fire near Gurugram. Two people were killed and 12 suffered burn injuries. July 1, 2023: On the Mumbai-Nagpur Expressway in Maharashtra, a sleeper bus hit a pole after a tyre burst. The diesel tank ruptured and the bus caught fire. Twenty-six people were killed. October 8, 2022: A private bus travelling to Mumbai caught fire after colliding with a truck in Nashik, Maharashtra. Twelve people, including a two-year-old child, were killed. June 3, 2022: A sleeper bus met with an accident near Kamalapur in Kalaburagi district, Karnataka. Seven people were burnt to death. Question 3: Why are sleeper buses banned in several countries? Answer: Sleeper buses are completely banned in several countries, including countries in Europe, the US, Germany, China and Australia. Their governments do not allow passengers to travel lying down or sleeping in buses. The reasons include bus design, international safety regulations and scientific analysis of accidents. Here is how it can be understood... 1. Mandatory seat-belt laws Strict UNECE (United Nations Economic Commission for Europe) rules apply in Europe and the US. Under these rules, three-point seat belts are legally required for every passenger on long-distance buses. 2. Risk of buses overturning Sleeper buses, particularly double-decker buses, are taller than conventional buses. On highways in Western countries, buses can travel at speeds of more than 100 kmph. At high speeds, these tall buses face a greater risk of losing balance and overturning while taking sharp turns. 3. Emergency exits can be obstructed Because berths are installed in sleeper buses, the aisle available for passengers is very narrow. Under Western safety standards, passengers should be able to evacuate safely within 90 seconds in the event of an accident or fire. With enclosed sleeper cabins, narrow passages and sleeping passengers, it has been found difficult to evacuate within this time during a panic situation. Most sleeper buses are double-deckers. Passengers sleeping in upper berths have even less time to climb down and exit the bus, increasing the risk of fatalities. 4. Scientific crash tests and data Crash tests by the European Transport Safety Council (ETSC) found that passengers sitting upright during an accident have an 80% higher chance of survival than those lying down. A passenger lying down may hit their head or legs directly against the bus structure, increasing the risk of neck and spinal injuries. Question 4: So why are sleeper buses not banned in India? Answer: There are several reasons. In simple terms, India’s transport system is quite different from that of Western countries. Here is how... 1. Heavy pressure on trains: Train tickets get booked weeks in advance during festivals. In such situations, sleeper buses remain an immediate alternative. Buses can also take passengers directly to their cities, villages and towns, which is not always possible by train. 2. Employment needs: India has a vast network of private bus operators. An immediate ban on sleeper buses could put the entire transport sector under pressure. 3. Changing lifestyles: Middle-class and working people prefer travelling at night during weekends and holidays to save time. Passengers can sleep on the bus and reach their workplace or home directly in the morning. This saves both hotel costs and valuable time. Question 5: So are there no rules or laws for sleeper buses in India? Answer: That is not the case. The Union Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has introduced strict rules and guidelines for sleeper buses. New regulations under AIS-052 (Bus Body Code) and AIS-119 (Sleeper Coach Standards) are aimed at preventing fire-related incidents. Earlier, local garages or unapproved vendors would convert seater buses into sleeper buses. This has been completely prohibited from September 1, 2025. Only automobile companies can now manufacture sleeper buses. An automatic fire detection and suppression system is also required in the engine compartment. It raises an alarm and sprays water as soon as it detects smoke or fire. The bus interior must use fire-resistant material so that fire does not spread rapidly. To reduce the risk of electrical short circuits, the battery box must be separately housed and provided with special protective shielding. Every sleeper coach must have at least four emergency exits. These include one wide emergency door and two escape hatches on the roof. Safety hammers must be installed in every cabin block so that passengers can easily break the windows, and the route to the windows must remain clear. Driver drowsiness alert systems or Advanced Driver Assistance Systems must be installed to alert drivers if they become sleepy at night. For safety and monitoring, buses must have at least three CCTV cameras and an emergency alarm system.

stories.summary: Subrat, the accused son of Kanpur millionaire businessman Vineet Minocha, has told police during his custody remand that he has “no regret” over having his father killed, alleging that Minocha was a “womaniser” who refused to give him money but spent thousands of rupees on women every Sunday. Speaking to the media on Thursday, Subrat said, “My father was extremely debauched. I killed my father because he was involved with women,” and claimed that he had paid his servant Vishal to murder Minocha and stage the death as an accident after Vishal refused, following which he planned to make it look like a heart attack. Subrat said he then told Vishal and Rajkishore that one would hold his father’s hands and legs while the other suffocated him with a pillow, but Rajkishore instead stabbed him to death with a knife. During the police custody remand, Subrat also told the police commissioner, “Sir, I have been thinking since the day of the murder that you would arrest me,” and said he deeply regretted Shalu being sent to jail, had started taking sleeping pills and, if he had not been arrested, would have taken sleeping pills and committed suicide. Read what emerged during the police custody remand… Daughter-in-law said: Leave my husband, let me stay in jail The servant had initially implicated Shalu, the businessman's daughter-in-law, in the murder. Shalu was subsequently sent to jail. The case took a turn on Thursday when it emerged that son Subrat had allegedly paid servant Vishal to kill his father. He had told him that if they were caught, Shalu should be framed. Despite this revelation, Shalu broke down in tears in front of police officials on Thursday. She told them, “Please release my husband. I am ready to go to jail in his place. I did not know that my husband was involved in my father-in-law's murder. If I had known this earlier, I would have taken all the blame upon myself.” Shalu's brother Dheeraj Arora, who had travelled from Lucknow, told Dainik Bhaskar in a conversation, “My entire family is shocked by the police's revelation. The whole family is wondering why Subrat did this. Subrat was also heavily in debt, and at Shalu's request, he was given ₹14 lakh a year ago.” Speaking about Subrat and Shalu's relationship, he said Shalu had informed the family about Subrat's addiction to alcohol and betting. Things returned to normal after some time. During the summer holidays, Shalu had gone to her maternal home. It was then that the family received information that Subrat had met with an accident after drinking alcohol. Shalu remained very worried about her husband's health. Has not seen son for 18 days, police arranged video call On September 6, police sent Shalu to jail on charges of murdering her father-in-law. Since then, her five-year-old son has been staying at his maternal grandparents' home. Whenever Shalu's brother Dheeraj Arora met her in jail, she would become anxious about her son. When Shalu was brought in for questioning on Thursday, she repeatedly appeared desperate to see her son even for a moment. She broke down several times while remembering him. When officials began questioning her, she told them, “Sir, please let me speak to my son once.” After repeated requests, officials arranged a video call between Shalu and her son. Shalu burst into tears as she called out her child's name. When the family tried to console her, she told her mother, “Please take care of my child.” Lawyer says Shalu's release will follow police application Shalu's lawyer Shivakant Dixit said that the legal team is now preparing for the police to file an application in court soon seeking Shalu's release from jail. Her release can then be secured on the basis of the application. Regarding Shalu's arrest, the lawyer said only the police could explain the circumstances at the time. In the present situation, it has emerged that Subrat had allegedly framed Shalu as part of a conspiracy, as revealed by the police investigation. Subrat made an elaborate plan to frame wife Shalu Police Commissioner Raghuveer Lal said Subrat had planned everything to implicate Shalu in the murder. He himself gave Shalu Vishal's phone number so that their conversations would appear in the call detail records. He would also take Shalu with him whenever he went to meet Vishal, ensuring that their locations appeared together. As part of the plan, he sent Shalu and Vishal together to Z Square Mall for shopping while he himself remained seated in the car. After the murder plan was finalised, Vishal bought a new SIM card on September 3 under the name Shubham. At 6.29 pm on September 3, Subrat called Vishal. The two spoke four times between 6.29 pm and 6.49 pm. Vishal switched off his old number on September 3. To make the suspicion of murder fall on Shalu, Subrat sent Vishal's new number to her on WhatsApp. On September 4, Janmashtami day, Vishal and Shalu spoke at 12.44 pm. Shalu had asked Vishal to bring new glasses and other items for Janmashtami. On the day of the murder, Vishal spoke to Subrat six times and to Shalu seven times. On the day of the murder, Subrat had told Shalu to tell security guard Madan Singh that Vishal's name was Shubham, which she did. Subrat's legal adviser had told him to stick to his statements The investigation revealed that Subrat had asked Vishal to get a duplicate key made for the flat. Vishal got a duplicate key made from Gumti No. 5 for ₹100. However, Subrat kept the key with himself. The flat door was opened using the original key. The Police Commissioner said that after Shalu's arrest, Subrat realised that he too would soon be arrested. He then came into contact with his family and lawyers. The Police Commissioner said that after the family learnt that Subrat could be implicated, they contacted a legal adviser. The legal adviser told Subrat, “Stick to your statements. The police will try to confuse you, but don't worry.” Spoke 258 times between May 1 and September 5 While collecting digital footprints, police found Subrat and Vishal's locations at several places before the murder, including Parade Chauraha, Gumti and Z Square Mall. Electronic evidence revealed that Vishal and Subrat had spoken 258 times between May 1 and September 5. Shalu and Vishal spoke 28 times between May 29 and September 4. Police also recovered several deleted chats from Subrat's mobile phone. Vishal's new number was saved on his phone under the name Shubham, while his old number had been deleted. This further deepened the police's suspicion. Subrat told police that he had himself sent Vishal's new number to Shalu on WhatsApp so that if she spoke to Vishal, the police would suspect her. He also told Shalu to tell guard Madan Singh that Vishal's name was Shubham on the day of the incident. When police recorded these statements, lasting 6 minutes and 22 seconds, and played them to Shalu, she was left completely stunned.

stories.title: Why Akhilesh started the ‘PDA Rath Yatra’ from Raebareli:Direct message to rebel MLAs; SP’s support base remains intact, entire Awadh region
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav has started the ‘PDA Rath Yatra’ for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Rae Bareli was chosen for a one-day trial run. The Samajwadi Party has not yet released a schedule for the districts the yatra will cover ahead of the election. The question is: Why target a Congress stronghold? The answer, according to the political calculations behind the move, is that the SP’s focus extends across the Awadh region. The choice of Rae Bareli is politically significant because it is associated with the Congress and is represented in the Lok Sabha by Rahul Gandhi. The move also comes against the backdrop of the 2024 Rajya Sabha election, when SP MLAs including Manoj Pandey, Rakesh Pratap Singh and Abhay Singh cross-voted in favour of BJP candidates. The SP later expelled the three from the party. By starting the yatra from Rae Bareli and mobilising party workers, Akhilesh is seeking to project the SP’s organisational strength in the region. However, there are five political factors behind the heightened activity in Rae Bareli. Let’s understand them one by one… 1. Attempt to strengthen its position in seat-sharing In the 2022 Assembly election, the Congress did not win any seat in Rae Bareli, while the SP won four. The BJP won the remaining two. Senior journalist Siddharth Kalhans says the SP wants to demonstrate its strength in the Gandhi family’s stronghold and strengthen its position at the alliance table. Under the usual logic of seat-sharing, giving up a seat held by a sitting MLA is not straightforward. There is also discussion that a formula could emerge under which the Congress symbol is used on some Rae Bareli seats while the candidate comes from the SP. Against this backdrop, Akhilesh’s outreach can be seen as an effort to establish the SP’s organisational and electoral presence before seat-sharing talks. 2. Build momentum across UP from Awadh Dalit, OBC and Muslim voters have a significant presence across the Awadh region. In Assembly seats in Rae Bareli, Amethi, Sultanpur, Barabanki, Unnao and Lucknow, communities such as Pasi, Lodhi, Yadav and Kurmi have a substantial presence. Akhilesh is presenting the Awadh region as an important testing ground for the SP’s ‘PDA model’. The party performed strongly in several Awadh districts in the 2022 Assembly election. For 2027, the SP is focusing on this belt as part of its wider organisational and electoral outreach. 3. Plan to take on rebel MLAs Manoj Pandey, a three-time SP MLA from Unchahar in Rae Bareli and former chief whip, Rakesh Pratap Singh, a three-time SP MLA from Gauriganj in Amethi, and Abhay Singh, a former SP MLA from Gosaiganj in Ayodhya, later moved towards the BJP. On September 24, Akhilesh referred to rebel leaders and said, “Those who run away will lose.” Political observers say the SP does not want to lose ground in these Awadh seats. Akhilesh is therefore reaching out to voters himself, seeking to project the party’s continued organisational presence in the region. 4. Message that the SP stands with its workers On September 17, a dispute broke out between Samajwadi Chhatra Sabha and ABVP workers at Feroze Gandhi Degree College in Rae Bareli. Harchandpur SP MLA Rahul Lodhi accused police of assault. UP minister Dinesh Pratap Singh, meanwhile, alleged that SP workers misbehave with officials. Akhilesh posted on X describing the incident as an “attack on PDA”. The dispute triggered a political exchange between SP and BJP leaders. During the PDA Rath Yatra, Akhilesh reached Rae Bareli and met the workers involved in the episode. 5. Mobilise crowds as in previous yatras The Rae Bareli programme is being presented as another major Rath Yatra-style mobilisation in Akhilesh Yadav’s political career. Previous campaigns, including the 2012 ‘Samajwadi Kranti Rath Yatra’ and the 2021 ‘Vijay Rath Yatra’, have been important parts of his political outreach. Political analysts say Akhilesh’s previous yatra also received a large response on the Rae Bareli-Lucknow route. The SP leadership is seeking to begin its 2027 campaign with a similar mobilisation of its cadre. Congress says alliance will not be affected; welcomes Akhilesh in its stronghold Congress spokesperson Surendra Singh Rajput says the party welcomes anyone working for backward classes, Dalits, tribals, women, young people, farmers and minorities. He says both the SP and Congress aim to end BJP rule in the state. According to Surendra Singh, no formal discussion on seat-sharing has started yet. SP sets target of increasing 27,000 votes in every Assembly constituency According to SP sources, Akhilesh Yadav has set a target of increasing the party’s vote tally by 27,000 in every Assembly constituency. The party is using the ‘Samajwadi Swabhiman’ app to connect with people at booth level. Recent reports also describe the SP’s ‘27 mein 27,000’ strategy as a booth-level mobilisation plan for the 2027 election. Through the app, families at booth level who did not vote in the 2022 or 2024 elections are being identified. Party workers are being assigned responsibility for reaching out to them and ensuring that they vote on polling day. The party’s control room will also monitor the process on election day.

stories.title: 9 burnt alive:Families cried over bodies after mother, brother remained unidentified; some identified by anklets
stories.summary: Nine passengers were burnt alive when a moving sleeper AC bus caught fire on the Yamuna Expressway in Noida on Wednesday night, leaving siblings Shivam and Nancy searching through badly burnt bodies for their mother Saroj Gupta and brother Mayank. At around 10 pm, the two had seen their mother and brother board the bus before returning home, but by morning they were outside the mortuary, where the bodies were so badly burnt that even identifying them was difficult; unable to find their mother and brother, Shivam and Nancy clung to each other and broke down, facing the question of which body they should look for their loved ones in. Similar heartbreaking scenes were witnessed outside the mortuary on Thursday. Some people had seen their loved ones off on a journey the previous night, only to arrive at the mortuary looking for them in the morning. In one case, a mother was battling for her life in hospital while the father had been burnt alive, and his body was in the mortuary. In another, a family identified their mother by the anklet on her foot. The fire had destroyed facial features, but small personal belongings became the last means of identifying loved ones. Such painful scenes emerged as several families searched for their relatives. Read the details ahead and also find out who is responsible for the accident. Three cases of families searching for their loved ones 1- Mother and brother put on bus at 10 pm, searched for them in the morning Shivam and Nancy reached the mortuary at around 10 am. They were looking for their mother, Saroj Gupta, and brother, Mayank. Initially, the two were not allowed inside. They were told that officials would arrive, the paperwork would be completed and the bodies would then be identified. The two siblings stood outside and kept crying. They asked every police officer they saw about their mother and brother. Each time, they were asked to wait. At around 2 pm, officials arrived, after which the two were taken inside. They spent around an hour trying to identify the bodies. However, the bodies were so badly burnt that identification was extremely difficult. For Shivam and Nancy, it was even difficult to determine which body might be their mother's and where to begin the identification process. 2- Son had gifted his mother an anklet, which helped identify the body Ayushi, the granddaughter of Usha Devi, also reached the mortuary looking for her. The most difficult moment for the family came when Usha Devi was identified by her anklet. The family said that her son had brought the anklet for her. The same anklet became the means of identifying her body after the accident. Once the identification was confirmed, the family broke down. Ayushi continued to cry outside the mortuary. Several bodies were badly burnt in the accident. For the relatives, identifying their loved ones has been no less than an ordeal. 3- They had left after grandmother's death; mother in hospital, father in mortuary Sarvagya had been searching for his father Devendra Bhardwaj since morning. He said that his father, Devendra, and mother, Rekha, had boarded the bus at Kashmere Gate in Delhi at night. His grandmother had died in Mahoba. His parents were travelling to attend the last rites. Devendra was a teacher at a university in Hisar and had retired from there. After the accident, Rekha was taken to hospital in an injured condition, but there was no information about Devendra. The family reached the mortuary in search of him. Devendra's body was later identified. His mother was admitted to hospital while his father's body was in the mortuary. Tears continued to flow from Sarvagya's eyes. Questioning the system, he said that they were not even being allowed to perform the last rites. Now the question of responsibility: Which officials are responsible? How did the bus continue to operate on the road despite so many challans? After nine deaths, the question is not only what caused the fire. The question is also how the bus continued to operate when it reportedly already had 19 traffic challans and around ₹1.75 lakh in outstanding fines. Officials have said that the bus's fitness certificate and permit were found to be valid. However, the fact that the bus had so many challans has raised questions about the role of the enforcement system. Responsibility: The main responsibility of the ARTO (Assistant Regional Transport Officer), Enforcement, is to ensure compliance with the Motor Vehicles Act on roads and take action against vehicles violating traffic rules. Negligence: The bus that caught fire had 19 challans for traffic rule violations. The total amount involved in these challans was around ₹1.75 lakh. Despite so many challans, the bus continued to operate. Responsibility: The enforcement department's main responsibility is to ensure compliance with the Motor Vehicles Act on roads and take action against vehicles violating traffic rules. Negligence: According to officials, the bus's fitness and permit were found to be valid. The question is why the bus was ignored despite having so many challans. Responsibility: Ensuring compliance with traffic rules in the city and issuing directions to traffic inspectors. Negligence: The bus travelled on this route every day. Despite this, no traffic inspector stopped it or checked the bus. No action was taken even after so many challans. Responsibility: Checking whether irregularities such as overloading, carrying passengers beyond the prescribed capacity, using an unauthorised route or stopping at unauthorised locations are taking place. Negligence: The bus had a seating capacity of 35. Officials said some passengers had left. This has raised the possibility that there were more passengers on board. The bus was not checked anywhere along the route. CFO says: Two drivers and one conductor arrested

This decision follows the withdrawal of CISF security services, which took place on May 4, 2026. The CISF had been providing security at the site since June 2015, after a violent incident. Investigators are examining potential connections to hostile state actors amid heightened security concerns.

Achieving over 200 wildlife crossings and safeguarding around 24 million hectares, Indigenous involvement is key to strengthening conservation practices here. stories.summary: California state officials secured 640 acres of desert land near Pioneertown for western Joshua tree conservation. Researchers identified this land as suitable for the species despite climate change. Collaboration with Native American tribes is planned for long-term stewardship of the property.

stories.title: Sister Stephanie Baliga: From aspiring elite runner to nun raising $2.6 million, and she’s still running

stories.summary: Private equity mogul Chuck Esserman has made headlines by purchasing a lavish mansion in San Francisco for $45 million, making it the most expensive home sale in the city for 2025. Formerly owned by Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison, who bought it for just $3.9 million 37 years ago, the estate boasts stunning renovations and breathtaking views of the Golden Gate Bridge, reflecting its rich legacy.

stories.title: Rhode Island federal judge orders revival of $7 billion Solar for All program canceled in 2025
stories.summary: A Rhode Island federal judge has ordered the revival of the $7 billion Solar for All program after the Trump administration’s EPA canceled it in August 2025. Judge Mary S. McElroy ruled the agency overstepped its authority in terminating the Biden-era initiative, which aimed to expand solar access for low-income households nationwide.

stories.summary: Hamas leader Yahya Sinwar reportedly sent a warning to Israel before the October 7 attack. Former defence minister Yoav Gallant stated that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu received international alerts about this threat. Gallant expressed that such warnings should have been prioritized as critical security issues. He claimed that Netanyahu excluded senior security officials from crucial discussions during the conflict.

stories.summary: Georgetown County School Board voted in favor of state plans to acquire two large land parcels for conservation. These lands would contribute to the creation of Carvers Bay State Forest and protect Arcadia East. The Board Member emphasized the importance of preserving natural spaces amid residential growth in the region. Conservation efforts received backing from local organizations and government councils expressing commitment to environmental protection.

3 killed, 4 injured after fight erupts into gunfire at Detroit strip club in US
stories.summary: Three individuals lost their lives while four others sustained injuries in a shooting at a Detroit strip club. The confrontation, which occurred early on Sunday morning, stemmed from an argument between several patrons. Detroit Police Chief Todd Bettison confirmed that the three deceased victims were all men. Authorities are actively investigating the case and have received multiple complaints about the venue this year.

stories.title: Charles Baker started garage business for his son in 1980; it has helped 12,500 plus workers
stories.summary: Charles P. Baker III, who died at 101, co-founded Baker Industries with his wife Louise in 1980 after their son struggled to find suitable work. What began as a two-person garage business grew into a workforce development nonprofit that has hired, trained and mentored more than 12,500 people who faced barriers to employment.

stories.title: Nepal battered by severe rain: 21 dead, 5 missing as floods, landslides worsen
stories.summary: In Nepal, heavy rainfall has caused devastating floods and landslides, resulting in 21 lives lost and extensive damage. Authorities have evacuated around 3,000 residents from perilous areas to guarantee their safety. This deluge follows the earlier Bhotekoshi floods, which had a death toll of over 1,400. As rescue efforts continue, landslides have disrupted operations in several districts, and tourists in vulnerable areas are being advised to take precautions.

The Colvins asserted ownership over a disputed 70-foot timberland strip, triggering rising tensions. Ultimately, the court sided with the Joneses, affirming the original boundary marked by an aged fence while ordering the Colvins to halt disruptive actions and compensate for damages.

stories.title: F-35 fighter jets, 200+ airmen arrive as US participates in India's Tarang Shakti air exercise
stories.summary: Six American F-35 fighter jets and over 200 US airmen arrived in Jodhpur to participate in Exercise Tarang Shakti. This exercise features the participation of more than 40 countries and strengthens international cooperation in military operations. US Ambassador Sergio Gor and Indian officials observed a joint demonstration by Indian and US Army personnel. The exercise emphasizes deepening bilateral training and trust among participating nations.

stories.summary: Pennsylvania teacher Ronald Sakolsky reunited with Chinese farmer Yin Yuzhen 26 years after donating $5,000 to support her tree-planting efforts in Inner Mongolia. His contribution helped Yin expand her work in the Maowusu Desert, which has since become a forest of around 50,000 trees, turning their friendship into an enduring environmental story.

This program offers complimentary lawn care services to seniors, veterans, and others in need. Through a digital platform, volunteers across all 50 states now connect with those requiring assistance, resulting in a thriving community of over 2,000 compassionate participants who collectively enhance the spirit of service and support nationwide.

stories.summary: At WorldSkills Shanghai 2026, India proudly secured the 10th position, reflecting remarkable strides in the global skills competition landscape. The nation earned six silver medals, demonstrating growth in a variety of fields. Significant first-time achievements in Dental Prosthetics and Digital Interactive Media Design were particularly noteworthy. With 70 competitors involved, India's investment in skill development is evident, promoting an enriched skilling ecosystem through global participation.

stories.summary: The Tamil Nadu government faced backlash after it issued a notification that exempted the Public (Law and Order) Department from the Right to Information (RTI) Act. SIR row: Jantar Mantar entrance barricaded ahead of protests; Gaurav Gogoi, others detained in Assam
stories.summary: Across India, demonstrations erupted as citizens rallied for the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. In Assam, Congress leaders confronted police barricades and were detained while protesting, even trying to set fire to an effigy of Kumar in criticism of his oversight of electoral rolls. Security in Delhi was bolstered in expectation of similar unrest, reflecting growing political tensions regarding the commission's recent actions.

stories.title: Georgia landowner's $23 million tax claim over 103 acres cut to $480,000 by court
stories.summary: A Georgia landowner claimed a $23 million charitable tax deduction after donating a 103-acre conservation easement, arguing the property could have been used as an aggregate quarry. The US Tax Court rejected the proposed quarry use, valuing the easement at $480,000. The 11th Circuit upheld the valuation and a 40% gross valuation misstatement penalty.

stories.title: ‘Dead mindset cannot see vibrancy’: Amit Shah hits back at Rahul’s ‘dead economy’ remark
‘BrahMos made in UP giving Pakistan sleepless nights’: Amit Shah hails India's growth 'despite adversities'
23 Himveers battle weeks of gruelling Himalayan climbing to reach 24,131-ft Mt Abi Gamin & unfurl Tricolour
stories.summary: At more than 7,000 metres, Abi Gamin presents a combination of thin air, freezing temperatures, snow and glacier terrain. Weather conditions can also change rapidly at such heights. The ITBP said the expedition demonstrated the force's mountaineering skills, determination and team spirit. After weeks on the mountain, the team finally reached the summit on September 16.

stories.title: Vote chori protest: Gaurav Gogoi, other Congress leaders detained; cops use water cannons in Patna, Chandigarh
Tennis icon Sania Mirza to lead Niva Bupa’s ‘Walk for Healthy Cities’ on September 27
Plea filed in SC against CEC Gyanesh Kumar over SIR decisions, seeks SIT inquiry
Ukraine strikes Russian oil refinery, train in overnight drone attacks; 2 killed
stories.summary: Russian governor Yuri Slyusar said around 50 drones were destroyed over the region and the strike forced the refinery to temporarily suspend operations. He said there were no reports of casualties there. In Ulyanovsk, eight people were injured after another drone attack damaged industrial and civilian infrastructure, Governor Alexei Russkikh said. The region is home to a major electronics plant.

stories.title: Colorado researchers grow world’s priciest spice on solar panels, doubling yield and earning $60,000
stories.summary: A study by Colorado State University reveals that saffron flourishes under semi-shaded solar panels, yielding better results than those without shade. By integrating rooftop farming with renewable energy, urban food production can tackle space constraints. Projections suggest considerable net revenue from saffron and electricity production in five years, although challenges related to installation and upkeep remain for successful implementation.

stories.title: Oregon buys 92-foot Abiqua Falls after fears it could be sold to a private owner
stories.summary: Oregon has approved a $2 million purchase of Abiqua Falls, a famous 92-foot waterfall that was put up for sale by its private owner in February. The deal includes 160 acres of land and will bring the waterfall under state ownership, while officials work on plans for management, maintenance and public access.

stories.title: US returns 36 Syrian antiquities worth $5M, including a Palmyra relief and 14 mosaics
51,000 reclining chair batteries recalled after reports of fires
stories.summary: The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission has recalled approximately 51,000 lithium-ion battery packs from Blue Cactus Company. These battery packs, sold on Amazon, pose risks of overheating and potentially catching fire. Consumers who purchased the recalled packs should immediately stop using them and contact the company for replacements. Proper disposal methods are required due to the fire hazard associated with these batteries.

stories.title: Veeramani Pocso case: Photo of TVK minister with Gem Granites chief surfaces; DMK says 'take action'
US mercenary, held at Myanmar camp, released from Tihar jail after NIA court's bail
stories.summary: While hearing the applications, the court noted that the accused had expressed their willingness to join the investigation whenever required by the NIA. The seven accused are Matthew Aaron Vandyke and co-accused Hurba Petro, Slyviak Taras, Ivan Sukmanovskyi, Stefankiv Marian, Honcharuk Maksim alias Maksym and Kaminskyi Viktor. The agency submitted that the immediate presence of the accused was not required.

stories.title: Selena’s 1995 family agreement; 31 years later, A.B. Quintanilla sues Suzette for $1M+
stories.summary: In a recent legal battle, A.B. Quintanilla III is taking his sister Suzette to court regarding the earnings from Selena's estate. Claiming entitlement to 25% of certain profits under a 1995 agreement, he alleges he hasn't received the complete payments for the past few years, while Suzette and their mother refute any accusations of misconduct, shedding light on the intricate handling of Selena's legacy.

stories.title: 'Must maintain the trust of people': Chirag Paswan urges EC to 'firmly present its side' amid SIR row
stories.summary: Union minister Chirag Paswan urged the Election Commission to take a firm stand amids rising criticism from opposition members. He highlighted the crucial need for the commission to maintain public confidence in the integrity of elections. In light of reported disagreements, opposition leaders are calling for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

stories.title: Nationwide protests from October 2 if Gyanesh doesn't resign by Saturday: CJP's Dipke amid SIR row
US Army ring lost in 2006 found in another soldier’s footlocker; returned to owner 20 years later
stories.summary: In a touching tale of serendipity, a silver US Army ring lost for twenty years has been reunited with its owner, Terry Sheppard Jr. Found by Mary Thelen in her son's footlocker, she took it upon herself to track him down. Douglas, who served in Iraq, probably misplaced it while stationed at Fort Bragg, North Carolina.

stories.title: Tarun Tejpal challenges rape conviction, SC seeks Goa govt response
'Gyanesh Kumar hatao, EC bachao': Congress puts up posters targeting CEC in Delhi
stories.summary: The Congress party has ramped up its protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, claiming that the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls is flawed. At a press conference, Rahul Gandhi voiced serious allegations against Kumar regarding electoral misconduct. Posters demanding Kumar's removal have been plastered around Delhi, alongside protests at the Election Commission.

stories.title: Meet Adrian Abraham, 9-year-old Indian-origin rock and metal guitarist aiming to set a world record
stories.summary: At just nine years old, Adrian Abraham is on a mission to pass a Grade 8 electric guitar exam in the UK, setting his sights on becoming the youngest achiever of this goal for a Guinness World Record. With a fervor for rock and metal music, he not only showcases his talents on stage but also creatively blends Indian music with Western rock on social media.

stories.title: Minnesota girl sends 100,000 Anne Frank-inspired bracelets across the world; earns $10,000 Young Hero Prize
stories.summary: At just 12 years old, Minnesota's Natalie Flaherty launched the 'I Stand With Anne' campaign, aimed at fighting hate in all its forms. She crafted more than 100,000 bracelets featuring her powerful message, spreading awareness across the globe. Through successful partnerships with organizations dedicated to Holocaust remembrance, Flaherty earned the prestigious 2026 Gloria Barron Prize. This passionate advocate plans to distribute more bracelets this Halloween, continuing her mission.

stories.title: An Italian town is rebuilding its school with 70% of the old building's demolition waste
stories.summary: A new primary school is being built in Castel Madama with a strong focus on sustainability and the use of reusable materials. About 70% of the waste from the existing school will be redirected to this project, promoting a circular economy. Designed with community needs in mind, the school will provide spaces for social and educational activities after hours. Accessibility is a priority, ensuring that all individuals can benefit.

stories.title: Massachusetts restores cranberry bog to protect rare trout that moves between river and ocean
stories.summary: Massachusetts is restoring Century Bog, a former cranberry farm in Plymouth and Wareham, to complete protection of Red Brook from White Island Pond to Buttermilk Bay. The restored wetland and stream channel could benefit about 60 conservation-priority species, including “salter” brook trout that move between freshwater and saltwater estuaries.

stories.title: Greg Norman bought an 8.3-acre Florida estate for $4.9M in 1991, then sold it 30 years later for $55.1M
Piles of elephant dung outside a Thai village became bricks for the Goya Tower
Why is Finland asking Musk to help Ukraine prepare for winter war against Russia?
stories.summary: Russian ballistic missile strikes reached record levels this summer, putting further pressure on Ukraine's already limited air defence resources. Patriot systems are currently the only Ukrainian air defences capable of intercepting such missiles, but Kyiv's stocks of interceptor missiles are severely depleted. Musk activated Starlink over Ukraine shortly after Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022.

stories.title: ‘Kashmiri Pandits driven out by Pakistan-backed terrorists’: India at UN
stories.summary: In response to Pakistan's statements at the UN Human Rights Council about Kashmir, Indian diplomat Kshitij Tyagi asserted that Jammu and Kashmir is an integral part of India. He denounced Pakistan's occupation of the territory while drawing attention to the systematic violence faced by religious minorities in Pakistan. Furthermore, Randhir Jaiswal dismissed Pakistan's assertions about the Indus Waters Treaty, reinforcing India's steadfast stance amid ongoing bilateral tensions.

stories.title: Bihar shocker: After Jamui, Samastipur, another girl harassed in public at tourist site
stories.summary: A video reportedly showing a minor girl being harassed in Banka has emerged online. Following this incident, police registered a case against six unidentified youths for their actions. The video appears to have been recorded six months ago at Mandar Parvat tourist site, according to initial investigations. Similar incidents in Samastipur and Muzaffarpur have previously led to multiple arrests.

stories.title: IIT Bombay suicide case: Crime Branch records statements of 20 people, NCSC conducts spot inquiry
stories.summary: The Mumbai Crime Branch has recorded statements from 20 individuals related to Sahil Wakode's death. Investigators have struggled to access details from Wakode's mobile phone, which is locked. The National Commission for Scheduled Castes is probing allegations of discrimination and harassment preceding his death. Wakode's family has demanded action against Professor Doolla while protesting at Azad Maidan. IIT Bombay has issued an apology regarding its earlier communications about the incident.

stories.title: ‘I kept crying, they held a knife to my neck’: 17-year-old gang rape at Delhi park
stories.summary: A 17-year-old girl experienced a disturbing incident on her birthday inside Aastha Kunj Park. After visiting Kalkaji Mandir, she and her friend were approached by three men claiming to be police officers. The men allegedly assaulted the girl at knife point in various locations within the park. After the attacks, they threatened her and her friend to remain silent about the incident.

stories.title: ‘Didn’t want to give credit’: Trump blasts CNN, MSNBC for skipping Xi’s White House welcome
stories.summary: Donald Trump asserted that CNN and MSNBC neglected to cover the significant visit of Chinese President Xi Jinping. He highlighted that these outlets face declining ratings due to their lack of credibility. Trump's comments were made regarding a ban on specific media organizations from White House grounds. A federal judge ruled that the ban was likely unconstitutional, reinforcing press freedoms.

stories.title: CJP Jantar Mantar protest: Woman's 'morphed' photo displayed alongside PM Modi; FIR
stories.summary: Riddhima Sharma, a 25-year-old woman, filed an FIR alleging her image was manipulated and used during a protest. She claimed unauthorized use of her photograph happened at a Jantar Mantar demonstration. The protest was held by the Cockroach Janta Party, where derogatory slogans were reportedly directed at her. Sharma identified several individuals linked to the protest but the FIR lists them as unidentified.

BJP spent 287cr in Bengal, 54% of total expense in 5 assembly polls

G4: UNSC losing its credibility, unable to maintain global peace
Opposition’s 3rd bid to remove CEC Gyanesh Kumar: Fresh motion likely, April 24 notice pending
At Studland Bay, replacing damaging boat anchors with eco-moorings cut scars in seagrass by 94%
stories.summary: At England’s Studland Bay, eco-moorings helped seagrass recover after years of damage from traditional boat anchors. A study found bare patches in one trial area shrank by 94% between 2021 and 2025. Volunteer divers have also reported rising seahorse numbers, along with sightings of eels, crabs and other marine life.
